jobs.title: Test Automation Engineer
jobs.description:
Halvik Corp
delivers a wide range of services to 13 executive agencies and 15 independent agencies. Halvik is a highly successful WOB business with more than 50 prime contracts and 500+ professionals delivering Digital Services, Advanced Analytics, Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning, Cyber Security and Cutting-Edge Technology across the US Government. Be a part of something special!

Position Overview

Halvik is seeking a Test Automation Engineer to support the U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) Office of the Chief Digital & Information Officer (OCDIO) Digital Factory capacity task order. Operating under DOT's IT Modernization Initiative (ITIM-2025-007) and the 2025–2029 "Path to 1DOT IT" strategy, the program delivers modernized, secure, and resilient applications through a Software Factory, Capacity-as-a-Service (CaaS) model. Halvik provides Agile Scrum teams for Development, Modernization, and Enhancement (DME) work across cloud, on-premises, and SaaS platforms hosted within the USDOT IT security boundary.

As a member of Halvik's DME Scrum teams, the Test Automation Engineer designs, builds, and maintains automated test suites that are embedded in the CI/CD pipeline and run with every build and release. The program's Mandatory Iteration-Level Testing & Validation Framework makes testing a required delivery control and calls for a progressive shift from manual to automated execution. This role drives that shift. It contributes directly to the end-client's objectives by catching defects early, protecting existing functionality through automated regression, keeping defect rates within contract thresholds, and producing the objective test evidence needed for the Definition of Done, release readiness, and Authority to Operate (ATO) packages.

Core Responsibilities

Strategic Execution: Lead the development of a test automation strategy and reusable framework for each assigned product, prioritizing automation of smoke, regression, end-to-end, and high-risk scenarios, and progressively converting manual test cases to automated execution in line with the program's Automation Transition Requirement.
Operational Oversight: Manage daily execution, maintenance, and triage of automated test suites. Monitor results, isolate flaky tests, investigate failures, and log defects with clear reproduction steps and severity in the Government-furnished Jira instance.
Collaboration: Coordinate with developers, the Senior Business Analyst / QA Analyst, the Cloud Engineer / DevSecOps / CI-CD, the Solutions Architect, and the Scrum Master to turn user stories and acceptance criteria into automated tests, build testability into features, and deliver tested increments every sprint.
Technical Performance: Integrate automated tests into CI/CD pipelines (e.g., GitHub Enterprise, Azure DevOps) so that tests run on every build, deployment, and promotion, and make results available for sprint demos, release readiness reviews, and ATO evidence packages.
Government-Furnished Tools: Configure and operate OCDIO's automated testing tool (currently ClicTest) and any other Government-furnished testing tools, adapting quickly when tools change or new ones are provided.
Test Coverage Across Categories: Build and maintain automated coverage across the required testing categories, including smoke testing in every environment (with post-deployment validation in Production), end-to-end workflows across UI, APIs, and data layers, persona and role-based permissions, regression, and integration/API contract testing.
Performance, Security, and Accessibility Testing: Support automated performance and load validation under realistic transaction volumes, security checks aligned to the OWASP Top 10 and authentication/authorization rules, and automated Section 508 (WCAG 2.0 A/AA) accessibility scans.
Evidence and Definition of Done: Ensure objective test evidence (executed scripts, logs, automated output, and pass/fail results) is attached to the corresponding Jira ticket before any item is marked "Done," and document the rationale for any testing category that does not apply to a given change.
Quality Metrics: Track and report automation coverage, pass rates, and defect trends, and help keep the defect rate below the program's five percent Maximum Allowable Defect Rate (MADR) while supporting any corrective action planning.
Data and Release Validation: Develop automated scripts to validate data migrations (record counts, transformations, field-level mappings) and to verify deployment and rollback procedures before production promotion.

Minimum Requirements

Education: Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Technology, or a related field.
Experience: Minimum of 5 years of professional experience in software quality assurance, including at least 3 years designing and maintaining automated test frameworks for web applications and APIs within Agile Scrum teams.
Technical Proficiency: Advanced knowledge of test automation tools such as Selenium, Playwright, or Cypress; API testing tools such as Postman or REST Assured; at least one programming language used for automation (e.g., Java, C#, Python, or JavaScript/TypeScript); Git; CI/CD integration with GitHub Actions or Azure DevOps; and Jira for defect and test evidence tracking.
Compliance: Must meet U.S. DOT contract requirements, including a favorable Public Trust background investigation and suitability determination.
Certifications: ISTQB Certified Tester (Foundation Level or Test Automation Engineer) or an equivalent testing certification is preferred.
Security Clearance: DOT Public Trust Clearance

Preferred Expertise

Demonstrated success in Federal Contracting, particularly civilian agency IT modernization or Software Factory programs; prior DOT experience is a plus.
Familiarity with ClicTest or other low-code/codeless automation platforms, and with Agile/Scrum practices such as behavior-driven development (e.g., Cucumber, SpecFlow).
Experience with performance and load testing tools (e.g., JMeter, k6) and automated accessibility testing tools (e.g., axe, ANDI); DHS Trusted Tester certification is a plus.
Experience automating tests for enterprise platforms used at DOT, such as Salesforce, Microsoft Power Platform, ServiceNow, Dynamics 365, or Appian.
Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities.

Privacy Policy – Halvik Corp

Benefits include 11 federal holidays and PTO

Eligible employees may receive performance-based incentives in recognition of individual and/or team achievements.

jobs.title: Sr Data Engineer
jobs.description:
The work we do has an impact on millions of lives, and you can be a part of it.

We help protect our customers against life’s uncertainties. Regardless of where you work within the company, you’ll be helping provide protection and peace of mind when our customers need it most.

Protective is looking for Data Engineers to design, build, and operate production data pipelines on Voyager, our Databricks lakehouse on Azure. You will own the end-to-end flow of data through a medallion architecture — ingesting source data into the Bronze layer, applying cleansing, validation, and conformance in Silver, and publishing trusted, consumption-ready data products in Gold.

This role sits at the intersection of engineering, analytics, and platform operations. You will write production-grade Python and SQL, enforce data contracts, and help Protective treat data as a product with named owners and real consumers. You will be embedded on a delivery pod that owns its data products end to end, rather than servicing tickets from a queue.

On Voyager, the medallion layers are named Raw, Prep, and Prod. They map directly to Bronze, Silver, and Gold and are used interchangeably in this description.

Key Responsibilities

Design, develop, and maintain production data pipelines on Databricks using Python, SQL, Apache Spark, and Delta Lake
Build Bronze-layer ingestion that reliably captures data from APIs, relational databases, flat files, cloud storage, and SaaS platforms — using dlt (dltHub) and Databricks-native ingestion where each fits — including incremental loading, pagination, watermarking, state management, and replay after failure
Develop Silver-layer transformations in dbt and Python over Delta Lake that cleanse, standardize, type, deduplicate, validate, conform, and enrich data so that it is reusable across domains. A meaningful share of this role is making messy source data trustworthy
Create Gold-layer data products: dimensional models, slowly changing dimensions, fact and bridge tables, aggregates, and serving tables aligned to how consumers actually query
Produce and maintain the curated datasets ML engineering trains and serves models from — feature and training tables that are versioned and reproducible, not one-off extracts
Author and maintain data contracts using the Open Data Contract Standard (ODCS) — schema with real semantics, named owner, known consumers, quality rules, and freshness expectations — and assess backward compatibility before every change
Implement data quality as code: uniqueness and not-null on keys at minimum, plus referential, accepted-value, freshness, and custom business-rule tests, surfaced to producers and consumers rather than buried in logs
Orchestrate ingestion and transformation as assets in Dagster, deployed to Dagster Cloud, and operate what you build across development, branch, and production deployments — schedules and sensors, asset dependencies, backfills, and run observability
Apply governance through Unity Catalog — catalogs, schemas, external locations, grants, row- and column-level security, and lineage — and handle credentials through Azure Key Vault rather than in code
Implement incremental and merge-based processing with Delta Lake (MERGE, schema evolution, time travel, OPTIMIZE) and tune Spark jobs, table layouts, and compute for performance and cost
Troubleshoot production failures, data-quality issues, source-system changes, and late-arriving or duplicate data — including backfills and recovery — and take part in the pod’s on-call rotation for the pipelines it owns, with root-cause analysis that closes the gap rather than reopening the ticket
Build and maintain CI/CD for data assets in Azure DevOps — automated tests and CI checks on dlt, dbt, and Dagster changes, promotion from development through branch deployments to production, and releases that are repeatable and auditable
Instrument what you own for observability: freshness, volume, quality, latency, and cost, with alerting tied to the SLAs and SLOs your contract commits to instead of depending on someone noticing
Work inside the platform’s control expectations — least-privilege access, secrets in Azure Key Vault, change management through pull request and pipeline, and audit evidence that falls out of the deployment path rather than being reconstructed later
Participate in code review and document architecture, runbooks, and data products so others can discover, trust, and reuse them
Work with data architects, analysts, product owners, and business stakeholders to translate requirements into maintainable data solutions

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related field; equivalent practical experience considered
3+ years building and supporting production data pipelines in a cloud data platform environment
Strong hands-on Python and SQL. Both are used daily and neither substitutes for the other
Hands-on experience with Databricks or a comparable Spark-based lakehouse, including Delta Lake tables, MERGE, and incremental load patterns
Practical understanding of medallion / multi-layer lakehouse design, and the judgment to say what belongs in Bronze versus Silver versus Gold
Experience ingesting data from APIs, relational databases, files, or SaaS applications, including the incremental and state-management problems that come with it
Working knowledge of dimensional modeling — grain, keys, facts and dimensions, slowly changing dimensions — and of ELT design patterns and data quality practice
Experience with orchestration and scheduling using Dagster, Databricks Workflows, Airflow, Azure Data Factory, or similar
Git-based source control, pull request review, automated testing, and CI/CD as normal practice — Azure DevOps or comparable
Experience troubleshooting production data failures, performance bottlenecks, and source-system changes
Experience with pipeline monitoring and alerting, and a working understanding of what a freshness or quality SLA means once real consumers depend on it
Ability to explain technical designs and trade-offs to both technical and non-technical partners

Preferred Qualifications

Databricks certification (Data Engineer Associate or Professional) or equivalent demonstrated depth
Unity Catalog experience: catalogs, schemas, volumes, external locations, storage credentials, permissions, and lineage
dbt on Databricks, or another transformation framework used alongside Spark
Python-based modeling frameworks over Delta Lake, and experience implementing Type 2 history, surrogate keys, and merge strategies in code
Experience with a declarative Python ingestion framework such as dlt (dltHub), Airbyte, Meltano, or Fivetran
Dagster experience specifically, including assets, asset checks, sensors, schedules, and branch deployments

Employee Benefits:

We aim to protect the wellbeing of our employees and their families with a broad benefits offering. In addition to offering comprehensive health, dental and vision insurance, we support emotional wellbeing through mental health benefits and an employee assistance program. Work/life balance is important and Protective offers a variety of paid time away benefits ( e.g. , paid time off, paid parental leave, short-term disability, and a cultural observance day). The financial health of our employees is just as important as physical and emotional health. Some of the financial wellbeing benefits include contributions to healthcare accounts, a pension plan, and a 401(k) plan with Company matching. All employees are encouraged to protect their overall wellbeing by engaging in ProHealth Rewards, Protective’s platform to improve wellbeing while earning cash rewards.

Eligibility for certain benefits may vary by position in accordance with the terms of the Company’s benefit plans.

If you require an accommodation to complete the application and recruitment process due to a disability, please email eric.hess@protective.com. This information will be held in confidence and used only to determine an appropriate accommodation for the application and recruitment process.

Please note that the above email is solely for individuals with disabilities requesting an accommodation. General employment questions should not be sent through this process.

new_jobs.description:
About The Team

API Multicloud partners with cloud service providers (CSPs) to bring OpenAI’s frontier models and APIs into the cloud environments where developers and enterprises already build. We own the API end to end across CSP platforms, from API integration and request routing through inference execution, capacity management, and day-to-day operations. Our mission is to make these capabilities available broadly and safely while preserving the reliability and developer experience customers expect from OpenAI.

Delivering that experience requires work across the stack: adapting API services and cloud-native integrations, bringing up model-serving environments, validating new releases, and operating the systems that connect customer requests to available capacity. We work directly with CSP engineering teams and partner closely with OpenAI’s inference, API, infrastructure, security, and Safety Systems teams. Together, we turn new model capabilities and partner requirements into dependable production services, with attention to performance, operational readiness, and efficient use of compute.

Our work contributes to OpenAI’s AWS partnership, including the launch of Daybreak Red and Daybreak Blue on Amazon Bedrock - and OpenAI’s newly announced Google Cloud partnership will bring our frontier models and Codex agentic workflows to Google Cloud’s Model Garden. These efforts let customers use OpenAI capabilities within the cloud infrastructure, security controls, and workflows they already rely on.

About The Role

We’re looking for experienced infrastructure engineers to design, build, and operate the systems that run OpenAI’s API across CSP platforms. You’ll help establish the cloud deployment platform: configuring and launching model-serving environments, planning capacity, improving caching and utilization, and making new releases safe and repeatable. Working closely with inference engineers, you’ll connect advances in model serving to the infrastructure and operational practices needed to run them reliably in production.

The role calls for strong distributed systems judgment and comfort moving across API services, cloud infrastructure, deployment tooling, and production debugging. You’ll work directly with CSP engineers to navigate differences in infrastructure, native services, and operating models, resolve integration issues, and build reusable solutions that reduce repeated work as we expand. Your decisions will affect how quickly new capabilities reach customers, how reliably they run, and how efficiently we use cloud resources.

In This Role, You Will

Design and build cloud infrastructure and distributed services that connect API requests, routing, and model-serving deployments.
Stand up and operate model-serving environments in partnership with inference engineers, bringing new models and serving capabilities into production.
Plan and manage cloud capacity, improving utilization, caching, request performance, and cost efficiency as demand grows.
Create repeatable build, release, and validation processes that catch functional and performance regressions before launch.
Develop reusable infrastructure abstractions that let API capabilities run consistently across CSPs while accommodating provider-specific requirements.
Partner with OpenAI’s inference, API, infrastructure, and security teams and CSP engineers to bring up the API serving stack on new platforms, resolve operational issues, and shape shared technical priorities.
Own production health through observability, incident diagnosis, reliability improvements, and practical automation.

Your Background Might Look Something Like

7+ years of experience leading cloud infrastructure or distributed systems projects from architecture through launch and ongoing production ownership.
Strong distributed systems fundamentals and the ability to reason about performance, reliability, and failure modes.
Hands-on experience building and operating services on a major CSP, including deployment systems, networking, storage, and cloud-native integrations.
Strong production coding and debugging skills, with the ability to move confidently through unfamiliar services and infrastructure.
Experience with capacity planning, performance optimization, or operational tooling for production systems at scale.
Sound technical judgment: you can turn ambiguous requirements into practical systems and reusable infrastructure.
Clear technical communication and experience working across teams or organizational boundaries to deliver complex projects.
Curiosity about model serving and AI infrastructure. Experience deploying models is a plus; direct ML or model-training experience is not required.

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. Built's Mission:
Connect and simplify doing business in real estate.

Built is the AI-powered platform transforming the way real estate is financed, developed, and managed. Purpose-built for real estate and construction, Built began by fixing construction draw management for lenders and has grown into a comprehensive operating system addressing some of the industry’s most complex challenges. Today, Built is a partner to more than 350 lenders, over 80,000 borrowers and owners, and thousands of contractors, powering 86,000 active projects valued at more than $300 billion. Learn more at getbuilt.com
.

__________________________

Innovation Software Engineer I, Marketplace

Built Technologies is the AI-first platform for construction and real estate finance, managing over $300 billion in annual capital for more than 340 lenders, including 45 of the top 100 U.S. banks.

Our technology helps financial institutions and construction companies manage the movement of capital throughout construction projects, from loan draws and inspections to payments, compliance, and portfolio risk. We're bringing modern software and AI into an industry where many critical workflows still depend on spreadsheets, emails, and manual processes.

This role sits on Marketplace
, a business unit focused on expanding Built beyond its core software into the services surrounding construction projects, including inspections, appraisals, insurance, and materials sourcing.

The team operates a little differently from a traditional engineering team. We're building the foundational technology that powers Marketplace while also experimenting with new products, getting early versions into customers' hands, and improving them based on real feedback.

As an Innovation Software Engineer
, you'll be part of that work from the beginning. You'll write code, build prototypes, experiment with AI-powered workflows, and learn how to turn customer problems into working software. You'll work closely with experienced engineers who will help you develop your technical skills, make sound engineering decisions, and gradually take on more ownership.

This is an opportunity for an early-career engineer who loves building things, learns quickly, and wants to understand not just how software works, but why it matters to the people using it.

The Team

Marketplace is a small, experienced engineering team that recently became its own business unit at Built. It's a collaborative group with a strong culture of mentorship, code review, and hands-on problem solving.

You'll work alongside Senior and Staff engineers, Product, Design, and business leaders, learning how new products go from an initial idea to something customers actually use.

What You'll Do

Build real software: Develop features, APIs, internal tools, and reusable components that support Marketplace products, working alongside experienced engineers on design, implementation, testing, and code review.
Prototype new ideas: Help turn early product concepts into working prototypes and MVPs. Build quickly, learn from feedback, and improve what you've shipped.
Build with AI: Use AI coding tools as part of your daily development workflow and help build AI-powered features, including document extraction, data validation, agent-driven workflows, and automation.
Learn production engineering: Develop your understanding of backend services, APIs, asynchronous workflows, data models, testing, and the practices that make software reliable and maintainable.
Get closer to customers: Participate in customer discovery conversations, observe how people use the products, and help translate what you learn into improvements.
Improve existing products: Identify friction in workflows, fix bugs, improve usability, and help make products more reliable and valuable for customers.
Automate manual work: Learn how a workflow operates before automating it, then build tools and integrations that reduce repetitive work and improve efficiency.
Grow your technical ownership: Participate in code reviews, ask questions, learn from feedback, and gradually take responsibility for larger pieces of engineering work.

What You'll Bring

0–2 years of experience in software engineering, product engineering, or a related technical role. Recent graduates and career changers with strong hands-on projects are encouraged to apply.
Experience writing code in TypeScript, JavaScript, or Python, whether through professional work, internships, coursework, or personal projects.
Familiarity with APIs, databases, and fundamental software engineering concepts.
Experience using AI coding tools or experimenting with LLMs to build something, along with curiosity about how AI can be incorporated into real products.
At least one project you've built that you can talk through, including the problem you were solving, how you approached it, and what you learned.
A genuine interest in building software, solving problems, and understanding how your work impacts customers.
Comfort learning unfamiliar technologies, asking for help, and incorporating feedback.
Strong communication skills and an interest in collaborating closely with engineers, Product, and other teams.

Nice to Have

Experience with React, Node.js, SQL, AWS, or other cloud technologies.
Exposure to LLM APIs, agent frameworks, RAG, document processing, or workflow automation.
Experience building side projects, contributing to open source, participating in hackathons, or launching something people actually use.
Internship or early-career experience in a startup, SaaS company, fintech, or another fast-moving technical environment.
Interest in financial services, construction, real estate, payments, lending, or other complex B2B industries.

What Success Looks Like At Six Months

You've shipped meaningful code or contributed to a working prototype that's being used by the team or real customers.
You're becoming comfortable navigating the Marketplace codebase, working with APIs and services, and following the team's engineering practices.
You've contributed to an AI-powered feature or automation and are developing good judgment about how to test and validate what AI produces.
You're beginning to own well-defined pieces of engineering work with less day-to-day guidance.
Your teammates see you as curious, dependable, collaborative, and someone who takes feedback seriously and keeps getting better.
You're developing an understanding of the customer problems Marketplace is solving and can connect your engineering work to those outcomes.

AI & Technology Expectations

Leverage AI tools to enhance the productivity, quality, and speed of your work.
Use AI to support drafting, analysis, summarization, and problem-solving across your role.
Identify opportunities to streamline workflows and reduce manual effort through automation and AI.
Apply AI to sharpen decision-making and strengthen technical and product insights.
Share effective AI use cases and best practices with your team.

The pay range is designed to accommodate upward mobility in the role, therefore it encompasses the full span of proficiency levels for this role and we believe that the midpoint of the range is competitive in the market. Salary is just one component of Built's total compensation package for employees; your total rewards package at Built will include equity, market-current medical, dental and vision coverage, an unlimited PTO policy, and other benefits.

__________________________

. Full-time offers are contingent on performance and business need.

Position Description

Ready to launch your software career? The Bluestaq Software Engineering Residency Program is an 11.5-week, paid, cohort-based program built around one goal: turning promising early-career developers into full-time Bluestaq Associate Software Engineers. This isn't a coffee-run internship. From week one you'll work real backlog items on the systems our U.S. Space Force customers use every day, guided by a dedicated engineer-mentor, and you'll close out the program by presenting your capstone work directly to Bluestaq engineering leadership.

Who We’re Looking For

We're offering the residency to early-career software talent ready to commit to a full-time engineering role, including: final-year associate, undergraduate, or master's students (graduating by January 2027), recent graduates in Computer Science, Mathematics, Cybersecurity, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Aerospace Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or related fields. If you're excited about learning fast, collaborating, and shipping real-world solutions, we want you on our team.

What You’ll Do

At Bluestaq, our residents aren't confined to one technology stack. You'll explore multiple technologies while contributing to impactful projects. Expect to work with languages and tools like Java, Python, Angular, Groovy, REST Services, GIT, PostgreSQL, Mongo, Athena, NiFi, Quarkus, and cloud platforms like Google Cloud, MS Azure, and AWS.

This isn't just about coding — we're all about growing your skills. You'll pair with experienced engineers, learn data storage solutions, front-end and back-end technologies, and cloud-based infrastructure, with structured milestones along the way: an onboarding week covering our tooling and secure development practices, a midpoint demo, and a capstone presentation. We offer the perfect balance of guidance and independence, allowing you to learn while making a real impact.

What Makes You a Great Fit

You have software development experience through coursework, personal projects, bootcamp work, or prior internships.
You have experience with software development and scripting languages.
You're familiar with front-end/back-end technologies, data storage solutions, and cloud platforms like AWS, Google Cloud, or MS Azure.
You're capable of working in a team-centric environment.
You have excellent verbal and written communication skills and a proactive approach to problem-solving.
You're passionate about big data technologies and excited to work with cloud infrastructures.
You have ability to obtain a security clearance.
You’re available to work full-time on-site for the full program (January 11 – March 31, 2027).

 Relocation assistance is available for full-time positions.

About Bluestaq

At Bluestaq, we build secure data platforms that matter for space missions, national defense, healthcare systems, and commercial innovation. Founded in 2018, we've become a leader in enterprise software and secure data management by staying focused on what counts: modern architecture, operational excellence, and mission impact.

We're engineers, problem-solvers, and builders who take the mission seriously, but not ourselves. We automate the repeatable, question the status quo, and design systems that are as reliable as they are scalable. new_jobs.title: Software Engineer, Integrations
new_jobs.description:
We're Scan.com. We're building America's national imaging network: the infrastructure that connects patients, providers, and payers to faster, better-value diagnostic imaging. Thousands of patients move through our platform every day, and each is a real person waiting for an answer to a healthcare concern. We exist to get them that answer faster.

We manage the medical imaging pathway end-to-end. Providers order through a single point of entry, and from there, we run the entire medical diagnostic pathway. Managing the full pathway, rather than brokering pieces of it, is what lets us deliver imaging faster, at higher quality, and at a lower cost than the fragmented status quo.

We're looking for a Software Engineer, Integrations,
at an exciting time. We've raised over $200m in funding to date, reached profitability, and are growing 100% year on year.

Millions of people wait too long for a diagnosis. Come help us fix that.

What You Will Be Getting Involved In

Scan.com's integration layer is mission-critical infrastructure. We interface with hundreds of imaging centers and health systems operating disparate, often decades-old systems — RIS platforms built on legacy protocols, HL7 v2 feeds with idiosyncratic vendor dialects, and hardware gateways running in constrained clinical environments. On the demand side, we connect to modern EHR APIs, third-party referral networks, and portal integrations that must work reliably at scale.

As a Software Engineer, Integrations
, you will architect and build the systems that make the demand-side connections robust, observable, and extensible. This problem area requires genuine passion for system integration patterns, message transformation pipelines, and the operational discipline to maintain high-reliability infrastructure in the face of real-world entropy.

Role

As a scale-up business, you can expect your role to develop over time. Here are some of the types of things you could be getting involved in:

Build and maintain integration connectors for modern and legacy EHR systems to retrieve physician referrals and relevant patient documentation.
Architect a fault-tolerant message queuing and delivery infrastructure for inbound and outbound HL7 and API traffic.
Build and maintain REST API integrations with third-party referral sources, attorney platforms, and demand aggregators.
Own the observability layer for the integration infrastructure: structured logging, alerting on message processing latency/failures, and dashboards that surface issues before they reach the operations teams.

THE TOP 5 THINGS WE WANT YOU TO ACHIEVE IN YOUR FIRST YEAR

Deep domain ownership. Within 90 days, you have a complete mental model of our integration workflows — every active connector, its transport mechanism, its failure modes, and its monitoring coverage.
Resilience uplift. You have identified and remediated the most critical reliability gaps in our referral pipeline. There is a measurable reduction in integration-related operational escalations.
Scalable transformation architecture. You have designed or materially evolved our data workflows such that onboarding a new demand-side source is a simple choice from a menu of robust technical options.
Observability in production. Every integration has structured alerting and a clear SLA. The operations team can self-serve integration health for routine issues without engineering involvement.
Shipped meaningful capability. At least two significant referral integration improvements. This can be new connectors that significantly increase referral volume, automations that improve quality, or infrastructure improvements. These improvements are live in production and have measurably increased referral volume, improved connection optionality, operational efficiency, and reduced error rates.

What You Might Bring To The Table

You don't need to tick all the boxes to apply for this role. Whether it's your first role or your fifth, we believe everyone can add value, learn, and grow. However, these might be some of the ways you are currently adding value:

Proven ability to integrate with legacy systems that were not designed for modern interoperability. For example, aging RIS platforms in radiology, core banking systems in fintech, or equivalent legacy infrastructure in another vertical. The underlying pattern of bridging old and new matters more than the specific domain.
Proficiency in at least one backend language used in high-reliability integration contexts (Python, Ruby, Java, C# are all relevant; language is less important than architectural rigor).
Familiarity with RESTful API integration patterns, including schema versioning, backward compatibility, and API contract management
Strong operational instincts: you instrument what you build, you think about failure modes before they happen, and you treat on-call escalations as a signal about systemic gaps
Bias for innovation: You care about questioning the ‘why’ behind every system, and have a strong desire to build the next generation of products you work on.
Experience in healthcare is a plus, but not required. We care far more about your engineering depth and API design fluency than your industry background

OUR VALUES

Always Play Offense

If we're not growing, we're dying. Everyone needs a bias for action. Speed and momentum, combined with quality execution, propel our business forward.

You don't quit on hard problems. Fail fast, dust off, go again.
You celebrate wins, then seek the next opportunity.
You see it, you fix it. No task is beneath you, at any level.

Build with the Best

The company we build is the team we build. If we don't have the right people in the right seats, doing the right things, we will fail.

Talent recognizes talent. You actively bring quality hires into the business.
You trust your colleagues to deliver.
You open-source your knowledge. You're never a single point of failure.

Care Deeply, Challenge Directly

Care enough to have the hard conversations, and don't dwell on them. Don't go up the chain to communicate. Go straight to the person.

Strong opinions, weakly held. You welcome challenge and feedback.
You get to the point: direct challenge plus an alternative solution.
You ask "why". Before calling something bad, understand why it exists.

Embrace Growth, Be Curious

Push the limits of your understanding and potential and you will be supported to get better.

You proactively seek feedback, whatever your level.
You invest in understanding our business: teams, customers, processes.
You invest in your own growth and are willing to unlearn.

We're a high-performing team with low ego. We hire people who are brilliant and kind, who give it straight, back it up with evidence, and change their mind when the facts change. We'll give you real ownership early, the tools to do the best work of your career, and colleagues who raise your game. In return, we ask for high standards, genuine care for patients and each other, and the drive to leave things better than you found them. If that sounds like you, let’s talk!

How We Will Interview You

We keep our interview process short and sweet, and we're a nimble team that can progress at pace. Here are the stages you can expect, but we might switch up the order of each step depending on team availability:

Introductory call/interview with our Senior Talent Partner. The call is via telephone and will last around 30 minutes.
Should it feel like there is an initial fit for all, we will invite you to a video call with the hiring manager for around 45 minutes. This is a more structured interview that will deep-dive into the role and technical needs.
'Scan Standard' interview, where our panel screens for values alignment and the success factors that matter at Scan.com. You will also be assessed on your AI fluency at the stage and depth relevant to your role (see AI Requirements above).
Meet the founders and/or other team members. Again, length varies depending on how many people and whether in person or via video call.
Offer!

What We Offer

We go beyond the basics with our benefits package. We believe great work starts with supporting our people. Here's what you can expect from us:

Salary range of $180,000 - $220,000
Flexible remote or hybrid work options
Dedicated personal development budget
Medical, vision, and dental coverage
28+ days of paid time off across PTO and wellbeing days, so you can show up at your best
Paid parental leave
401k retirement plan
All the equipment you need to do your best work
Inclusive, people-first policies designed by our team, for our team

DIVERSITY AT
SCAN.COM

Scan.com is committed to eliminating discrimination and encouraging diversity within our team. We strive to provide equality and fairness for all job applicants and employees and never discriminate on the basis of gender, marital status, age, race, ethnicity, religion, or physical differences.

We are opposed to all forms of unlawful treatment and discrimination.

Our ambition is for our team to be representative of society's diversity, and for every employee to feel respected and able to bring their best selves to work.

If you need an accommodation to apply or interview, contact us at people@scan.com.

We look forward to receiving your application!

At PNNL, our core capabilities are divided among major departments that we refer to as Directorates within the Lab, focused on a specific area of scientific research or other function, with its own leadership team and dedicated budget.

The AI and Data Analytics Division, part of NSD, combines profound domain expertise and creative integration of advanced hardware and software to deliver computational solutions that address complex data and analytic challenges. Working in multidisciplinary teams, we connect foundational research to engineering to operations, providing the tools to innovate quickly and field results faster. Our strengths are integrated across the data analytics lifecycle, from data acquisition and management to analysis and decision support.

new_jobs.title: Software Test & Automation Engineer  II
new_jobs.description:
Quantum Space is redefining mobility and maneuverability in space. Our high-mobility spacecraft platforms support national security, civil, and commercial missions with unmatched flexibility and propulsion capability. We build fast and iterate quickly.

Who We’re Looking For

We are seeking a skilled and motivated Software Test & Automation Engineer II
to develop and maintain automated testing solutions that ensure the reliability, functionality, and performance of our next-generation spacecraft flight software. In this role, you will contribute to software integration, verification, and regression testing by developing automated test frameworks, requirements-based test cases, and test scripts that validate mission-critical spacecraft functions.

You will work closely with flight software, systems engineering, and integration and test teams to support software testing across software-in-the-loop (SIL), hardware-in-the-loop (HIL), and flight-representative environments. This position is ideal for an engineer with strong programming and test automation skills who thrives in a fast-paced environment, enjoys solving complex technical challenges, and is passionate about building reliable software for next-generation space missions.

Where You’ll Make an Impact

Develop and maintain automated integration, verification, and regression testing capabilities for spacecraft flight software.
Design, implement, and execute requirements-based test cases and automated test scripts to validate flight software functionality and performance.
Develop and enhance automated test frameworks using Python, C/C++, or equivalent programming languages.
Verify spacecraft command and telemetry processing, mode management, fault management, and other critical flight software functions.
Support software testing in software-in-the-loop (SIL), hardware-in-the-loop (HIL), and flight-representative environments.
Collaborate with flight software developers, systems engineers, and integration and test teams to identify defects, troubleshoot issues, and support root-cause analysis.
Develop and maintain automated regression test suites to ensure software changes do not impact existing functionality.
Integrate automated testing into CI/CD pipelines to improve software quality, testing efficiency, and development workflows.
Analyze test results, document defects, and generate verification reports to support software readiness and requirements compliance.
Support the development and maintenance of software test environments, simulation tools, and test infrastructure.
Participate in technical reviews and contribute to improvements in software verification processes, automation tools, and configuration management practices.

What It Takes

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related technical field.
2+ years of experience in software development, software testing, test automation, or a related engineering discipline.
Strong programming skills in Python, C/C++, or equivalent languages.
Experience developing automated test scripts, test frameworks, or software verification tools.
Experience testing embedded systems, real-time software, or complex software applications.
Understanding of software integration, verification, validation, and regression testing methodologies.
Familiarity with automated testing, CI/CD processes, and software configuration management practices.
Experience with software debugging, troubleshooting, and defect tracking.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills with the ability to work effectively in a collaborative engineering environment.

Nice-to-Have Experience

Experience with spacecraft flight software, satellite systems, avionics, or other mission-critical embedded software.
Familiarity with spacecraft flight software architectures, command and telemetry processing, mode management, and fault detection and recovery.
Hands-on experience with software-in-the-loop (SIL) and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) testing environments.
Experience developing automated test frameworks using Python, pytest, or similar testing tools.
Experience working with real-time operating systems (RTOS), embedded Linux, or similar environments.
Familiarity with spacecraft simulation tools, ground support equipment, or flight-representative test environments.
Experience with CI/CD tools such as Jenkins, GitLab CI/CD, or GitHub Actions.
Experience with Git, JIRA, or similar software development and configuration management tools.
Understanding of requirements traceability, test coverage analysis, and software verification and validation (V&V) processes.
Experience supporting spacecraft integration and testing, software qualification, or mission readiness activities.

What You’ll Get

Ownership – Develop and maintain automated testing solutions that directly contribute to the reliability and performance of mission-critical spacecraft flight software.
Innovation – Support transformative aerospace and defense programs enabling next-generation space mobility and operations.
Impact – Help ensure spacecraft flight software meets critical performance, reliability, and mission readiness requirements through automated verification and testing.
Growth – Join a collaborative engineering team working across flight software, systems engineering, and spacecraft integration and testing in a fast-paced, innovative environment.
Compensation – Competitive salary, equity, and comprehensive benefits including medical, dental, vision, generous leave, FSA, 401(k) matching, and equity sharing.

Location:
Rockville, MD

Base Salary:
$100,000-140,000

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Quantum Space's total compensation package.

Additional Requirements

To comply with U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including ITAR, applicants must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident, protected individual per 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.

Apply now. Join us in building the next generation of spacecraft.

In this role, you would support the development of software solutions and data-driven tools that enhance FANUC America's robotic paint and sealer systems. As part of the PSH Software Engineering team, you would contribute to the design, development, testing, implementation, and support of software products used in advanced industrial automation environments. You would collaborate with Controls Engineers, Process Engineers, and project teams to develop software applications, reporting tools, dashboards, automation workflows, and data analysis solutions. Success in this role requires strong analytical thinking, software development expertise, attention to detail, and a passion for solving complex technical challenges. If you enjoy working at the intersection of software engineering, data analysis, and industrial automation, we encourage you to apply.

How It's Done

Support the full software engineering lifecycle for new and existing robotic paint and sealer system products.
Design, develop, test, and implement software applications and product enhancements.

Job Title: Embedded Software Engineer

Job Description

This role focuses on designing and developing embedded software for weapon control systems within a broader Battle Management System portfolio. You will work on multiple projects, ranging from coding on embedded microcontrollers to building simulators with interactive graphical user interfaces. The position includes supporting the installation and assessment of embedded systems both locally and at external locations. You will collaborate closely with a team of approximately 15 engineers on a large, complex program, contributing to mission-critical capabilities.

Responsibilities

Design, code, and engineer embedded software solutions for weapon control systems across multiple Battle Management System projects.
Develop software for embedded microcontrollers, ensuring reliable and efficient operation in real-time environments.
Create simulators and interactive graphical user interfaces to support system development, testing, and demonstration.
Debug and troubleshoot low-level hardwaresoftware interfaces using tools such as oscilloscopes and logic analyzers.
Diagnose and resolve network-related issues, including network configuration, connectivity, and data transmission problems.
Write test cases and perform unit testing to validate hardwaresoftware integration and overall system functionality.
Support installation, integration, and assessment of embedded systems at local and external test and operational sites.
Work effectively in a fast-paced, rapidly changing range and field environment with a strong focus on fielding a reliable product.
Support tasking across multiple concurrent projects, managing priorities and collaborating with cross-functional team members.
Use version control systems and modern development tools to maintain code quality, traceability, and configuration control.

Essential Skills

Minimum of three (3) years of experience demonstrating the ability to concept, prototype, design, code, and engineer embedded software solutions.
Bachelor of Science degree from an accredited college or university in computer engineering or electrical engineering, or equivalent direct hands-on experience with a weapon system application.
Proficiency in at least one of the following programming languages: C#, Java, or C++.
Knowledge of hardware architectures, microcontrollers, and communication protocols relevant to embedded systems.
Knowledge of graphical user interface (GUI) development, including design and implementation.
Knowledge of the TCP/IP protocol suite, including network stack integration and socket programming.
Proficiency with widely used version control systems, such as Git.
Experience using debugging and troubleshooting tools for embedded systems and low-level hardwaresoftware interfaces.
Ability to work in a fast-paced environment and support multiple projects simultaneously.
Eligibility to obtain and maintain a Secret security clearance

Additional Skills & Qualifications

Knowledge and experience with weapon system integration.
Knowledge, experience, and understanding of military standards such as MIL-STD-1553.
Experience integrating embedded systems with GPS, sensors, safety interlock circuitry, and other mission-critical subsystems.
Experience with Linux-based environments for development or deployment of embedded solutions.
Familiarity with real-time operating systems (RTOS) for embedded applications.
Experience with modern development platforms and collaboration tools, including Git-based repositories and continuous integration systems.
Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to diagnose complex issues involving hardware, software, and networks.
Effective communication skills and the ability to collaborate within a multidisciplinary engineering team.

Work Environment

This position is fully onsite, five days a week, at a base in Dahlgren, VA. You will work within a secure facility as part of a team of approximately 15 engineers on a large, prime weapon system program. The environment is fast paced and field oriented, with frequent interaction between software, hardware, and test personnel. You will use tools such as oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, embedded development environments, version control systems, and network analysis utilities. Work involves both laboratory and range or field settings, with a strong focus on delivering reliable, deployable products in support of mission-critical operations.

Job Description

Your Work Shapes the World at Caterpillar Inc.

When you join Caterpillar, you're joining a global team who cares not just about the work we do – but also about each other. We are the makers, problem solvers, and future world builders who are creating stronger, more sustainable communities. We don't just talk about progress and innovation here – we make it happen, with our customers, where we work and live. Together, we are building a better world, so we can all enjoy living in it.

Help Build the Future of Caterpillar –

At Caterpillar, technology always has a purpose, which is to solve our customers’ toughest challenges. Through Cat Technology, we are solving problems by building the intelligence layer that connects machines, data, and people to make jobsites safer, more productive, and more sustainable. By combining deep domain expertise in physical systems with software, connectivity, autonomy, and AI, we deliver solutions that work in the real world—on real jobsites, at global scale.

You’ll build and deploy against one of the most unique data foundations—over 1.6 million connected assets generating real-world data daily. These data and platform capabilities are enabling the development of AI models, edge computing architectures, and software systems that scale across fleets, products, and industries. The result will be a new generation of machines that continuously learn, improve, and deliver performance at scale.

Be Part of What’s Next in Autonomous Construction Sites

Construction autonomy is one of the most complex challenges in applied AI, and at Caterpillar, advancements in physical AI, simulation, sensing, and edge computing are turning things that once felt impossible—intelligent machines operating in dynamic jobsites—into reality.

Our connected ecosystem brings together massive volumes of high-quality data to create a foundation where engineers like you can build and deploy against.

If this work motivates you, we invite you to join our team. In these roles, you’ll work at the intersection of the physical and digital worlds. You’ll help design and deliver intelligent systems that enable machines to perceive their environment, make informed decisions, and support safer, more productive operations.

Apply today to build the new era of construction autonomy at Caterpillar.

We are seeking an AI Automation Engineer to develop annotation automation solutions used to create training data for robotics, autonomy, computer vision, and Vision-Language-Action (VLA) systems with a scrum team.

This role combines software engineering, machine learning, and data engineering to build automated annotation and captioning capabilities for real-world heavy equipment and construction environments. You will help deploy and extend technologies such as NVIDIA Cosmos Curator and Cosmos Reason while also developing Caterpillar-specific AI models that enable automated labeling, automated captioning, and AI-driven quality assurance.

This is a hands-on technical role focused on turning complex AI and data challenges into scalable production solutions.

Develop and deploy automated labeling and captioning solutions for perception and VLA datasets.
Train, fine-tune, and evaluate AI models to support auto-labeling, auto-captioning, and annotation quality automation.
Build data pipelines and workflows that move datasets through automated labeling, human review, quality validation, and dataset publication.
Implement and extend platforms such as NVIDIA Cosmos Curator, Cosmos Reason, and other emerging AI automation technologies.
Develop solutions that integrate Caterpillar data systems with external annotation providers and human-in-the-loop workflows.
Ensure reliability, scalability, observability, and operational excellence across annotation automation services.

What Makes This Role Unique

Most AI automation solutions are not trained to understand heavy equipment, jobsites, sensor data, or machine operations.

In this role, you'll help develop the AI capabilities needed to label and describe Caterpillar-specific data at scale. You'll work on challenges involving computer vision, multimodal AI, robotics, autonomy, and Vision-Language-Action systems while helping create the data foundation that powers the future of intelligent machines.

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Robotics, or a related field.
Experience developing production-grade software solutions using Python, modern software engineering practices and containerization platforms (e.g. Docker, Kubernetes)
Experience designing and implementing distributed systems, APIs, and data processing pipelines.
Experience training, fine-tuning, or deploying machine learning models.
Strong problem-solving skills and ability to work across multiple technical disciplines.
Experience generating and managing camera and LiDAR sensor datasets for perception or machine learning applications, including data collection pipeline design and ground truth generation.
Experience in data annotation and quality assurance for autonomous systems or computer vision projects, with demonstrated ability to define annotation guidelines, identify labeling defects, and drive measurable improvements in dataset accuracy.
Experience using annotation and dataset management tools such as Labelbox, Supervisely, RoboFlow or similar toolchains.
Experience using machine learning frameworks and training tools such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, ONNX, Weights & Biases, MLflow or similar frameworks.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with computer vision, robotics, autonomy, Physical AI, or multimodal AI systems.
Experience with AI-assisted annotation, auto-labeling, or machine learning data pipelines.
Experience training or fine-tuning foundation models, vision models, or multimodal models.
Experience with NVIDIA Cosmos Curator, Cosmos Reason, or similar AI automation platforms.

Experience with sensor data such as cameras, LiDAR, radar, or autonomous machine datasets.

Experience building human-in-the-loop AI workflows and quality automation systems.

You'll work on some of the most challenging applications of AI in the physical world, helping build systems that transform vast amounts of machine and sensor data into the intelligence that powers autonomous and AI-enabled equipment. Our partner is seeking a Software Engineer II to join a Decision Management Program team responsible for an enterprise notification platform supporting high-volume transaction processing and customer-facing communications.

The platform processes transaction events and delivers notifications through email, SMS, and API channels. Engineers on the team develop and maintain distributed, event-driven services that support critical fraud prevention, security, and customer engagement products.

As a Software Engineer II, you will contribute to the design, development, testing, deployment, and production support of backend services that power the notification platform. You will work closely with Product, Technical Program Management, Architecture, Quality Assurance, and partner engineering teams to deliver scalable, resilient, secure, and maintainable software solutions.

The ideal candidate has a strong foundation in Java and Spring Boot development, REST APIs, microservices, and software engineering principles. Experience with Kafka, distributed event-driven architectures, cloud-native technologies, and high-volume transaction processing environments is highly preferred.

Design software components and service interactions that support scalability, maintainability, reliability, and performance requirements.

Join us to discover a culture that is rooted in innovation and thrives on collaboration. Imagine loving what you do and where you do it.

The actual salary for this position will be determined by a number of factors, including the scope, complexity and location of the role; the skills, education, training, credentials and experience of the candidate; and other conditions of employment. 1

Travelers is seeking a Software Engineer II to join our organization as we grow and transform our Technology landscape. As a member of the Observability team, you will join a team focused on improving system reliability and mean-time-to-resolution for our Business Insurance applications. We’re looking for an experienced observability engineer with expertise in Dynatrace and OpenTelemetry who can decompose business processes into observability requirements, define alerting and dashboards scoped to business impact, and act a subject matter expert for application teams.

Perform other duties as assigned.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

Four years of programming/development experience.

Domain Expertise - Demonstrated track record of domain expertise including understanding technical concepts necessary to do the job effectively and aware of industry trends, demonstrate willingness, cooperation, and concern for business issues and priorities, and possess in depth knowledge of immediate systems worked on and some knowledge of adjacent systems.
Problem Solving - Strong problem solver who ensures solutions are built for the long term, is able to resolve new issues, recognizes mistakes using them as learning and teaching opportunities and consistently breaks down large problems into smaller, more manageable ones.
Communication - Strong communicator who possesses the ability to articulate information clearly and concisely with the business, document work in a clear, easy to follow manner, collaborate well with team members as both a mentor and mentee, take in vague requirements and ask the right questions to ensure clarification, offer feedback appropriately and effectively, seek out and receives constructive criticism well, listen when others are speaking and make space for colleagues to share their thoughts.

Travelers is an equal opportunity employer. We value the unique abilities and talents each individual brings to our organization and recognize that we benefit in numerous ways from our differences.

new_jobs.title: Machine Learning Engineer, Growth Platform
new_jobs.description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About The Team

Growth Platform builds the machine learning systems that help businesses discover and use the Stripe products that meet their needs. Our recommendations reach users across the Dashboard, email, onboarding, documentation, and AI agent interfaces. We combine an understanding of each business with models that decide which recommendation is useful, when to show it, and how to learn from the outcome.

Our work spans recommendation and ranking models, contextual bandits, agent-based recommendations, and the data and evaluation systems behind them. We build shared capabilities that product, marketing, and sales teams can use across Stripe. Success means helping businesses take useful actions and adopt products that help them grow, while keeping recommendations relevant and avoiding unnecessary messages.

What you’ll do

You will build and operate production ML systems that improve how Stripe recommends products, content, and next steps to businesses. You will own work from problem definition and feature development through training, evaluation, deployment, monitoring, and iteration. Working with data scientists, engineers, and product partners, you will turn model improvements into measurable user and business outcomes.

Responsibilities

Design, train, evaluate, deploy, and maintain models for recommendation, ranking, and personalized action selection across Growth Platform surfaces.
Improve contextual bandit and policy-learning approaches, including exploration, reward design, and how recommendations adapt to user context and feedback.
Build agent-based recommendation capabilities that use business context to identify relevant products and integration options, with evaluations that test recommendation quality and usefulness.
Develop reliable data and feature pipelines for training and inference. Improve data freshness, feature quality, and consistency between training and production.
Build reusable tooling for model evaluation, retraining, and safe rollout so the team can test and ship improvements faster.
Own the quality and operation of the team's ML components: write tested production code, monitor models and pipelines, investigate failures, and improve reliability, latency, and cost.
Design and analyze online experiments with data science partners. Connect offline evaluation to product adoption and incremental impact, with guardrails for dismissals, unsubscribes, and user experience.
Partner with product engineering to integrate models into recommendation delivery systems, and with ML infrastructure teams to use and improve Stripe's shared training, feature, and serving capabilities.
Work with product, marketing, and sales partners to identify problems that shared ML capabilities can solve, and make practical choices about where modeling adds value.

Who you are

You are a machine learning engineer with a builder mindset. You care about the business problem, the quality of the model, and what happens after it ships. You can move between modeling and software engineering, make practical tradeoffs, and take ownership of an ambiguous problem through production and measurement.

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum Requirements

3+ years of industry experience in machine learning engineering, software engineering, or applied data science, with hands-on experience building and shipping ML models in production.
Strong programming skills in Python and experience writing maintainable, tested production code.
Practical experience designing, training, and evaluating ML models using frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, XGBoost, or scikit-learn.
Experience building data or feature pipelines, proficiency in SQL, and familiarity with distributed data processing tools such as Spark or PySpark.
A strong understanding of statistics, model evaluation, and experimentation, including the ability to recognize data leakage and distinguish offline model improvements from business impact.
Experience deploying, monitoring, and debugging production ML systems, and evaluating tradeoffs among model quality, reliability, latency, and cost.
Ability to turn an open-ended business problem into a technical approach and collaborate effectively with engineering, data science, product, and business partners.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with recommendation systems, ranking, personalization, or marketplace and advertising optimization.
Experience with contextual bandits, policy learning, causal inference, or off-policy evaluation.
Experience building and evaluating LLM applications, including structured extraction, embeddings, or recommendations grounded in user and business context.
Experience building reusable ML capabilities used by multiple products or teams, including training automation, feature systems, or model monitoring.
Experience with product growth, lifecycle messaging, or systems that balance short-term engagement with longer-term user outcomes.

Hybrid work at Stripe

This role is available either in an office or a remote location (35+ miles or 56+ km from a Stripe office).

In-office expectations

Office-assigned Stripes spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. This hits a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility about how to do this in a way that makes sense for individuals and their teams.

Working remotely at Stripe

A remote location is defined as being 35 miles (56 kilometers) or more from one of our offices. While you would be welcome to come into the office for team/business meetings, on-sites, meet-ups, and events, our expectation is you would regularly work from home rather than a Stripe office. Stripe does not cover the cost of relocating to a remote location. We encourage you to apply for roles that match the location where you currently live or plan to live.

Pay and benefits

The annual US base salary range for this role is $180,000 - $270,000. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. This salary range may be inclusive of several career levels at Stripe and will be narrowed during the interview process based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and location. Applicants interested in this role and who are not located in the US may request the annual salary range for their location during the interview process.

Additional benefits for this role may include: equity, company bonus or sales commissions/bonuses; 401(k) plan; medical, dental, and vision benefits; and wellness stipends.

We look forward to hearing from you.

At Stripe, we're looking for people with passion, grit, and integrity. You're encouraged to apply even if your experience doesn't precisely match the job description. Your skills and passion will stand out—and set you apart—especially if your career has taken some extraordinary twists and turns. At Stripe, we welcome diverse perspectives and people who think rigorously and aren't afraid to challenge assumptions. Join us.

Apply now

Description

About Us

Headquartered in the United States, TP-Link Systems Inc. is a global provider of reliable networking devices and smart home products, consistently ranked as the world’s top provider of Wi-Fi devices. The company is committed to delivering innovative products that enhance people’s lives through faster, more reliable connectivity. With a commitment to excellence, TP-Link serves customers in over 170 countries and continues to grow its global footprint.

We believe technology changes the world for the better! At TP-Link Systems Inc, we are committed to crafting dependable, high-performance products to connect users worldwide with the wonders of technology.

Embracing professionalism, innovation, excellence, and simplicity, we aim to assist our clients in achieving remarkable global performance and enable consumers to enjoy a seamless, effortless lifestyle.

Overview:

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Build, run, and own ETL pipelines on EMR (Spark) orchestrated in Airflow — including their monitoring, alerting, and recovery.
Write SQL and Python for data ingestion, transformation, and the datasets that analysts and dashboards depend on.
Own data quality for what you build — run the checks before you ship and add new ones where they're missing; confirm the results are correct, not only that the job completed.
Build and extend the data models for your area: fact and dimension tables following the team's layering conventions.
Keep your jobs efficient — watch runtime and cost, and raise slow or expensive jobs rather than living with them.
Use and extend the team's shared patterns and templates, and turn work you find yourself repeating into something automated or reusable.
Work with analysts and business stakeholders to turn requests into datasets that actually get used.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

2–4 years of hands-on data development in a production environment — pipelines that run on a schedule with real downstream consumers, that you were responsible for including when they broke.
Strong SQL: window functions, complex multi-table joins, incremental loads, and the ability to work out why a query is slow.
Python for production ETL and tooling (PySpark, pandas, boto3) — code that runs on a schedule, not only notebooks.
Hands-on experience with Spark on a cloud platform: AWS EMR, Databricks, Glue, or equivalent.
Production experience with a scheduler, Airflow preferred: DAG design, dependencies, retries, and reruns that are safe to repeat.
Working understanding of dimensional modeling: fact and dimension tables, star schema, and warehouse layering.
Comfortable working on AWS (S3 with Parquet / ORC), Linux, and Git — and comfortable picking up new tools as the platform evolves.
Effective use of AI to solve data problems — using it to move faster on SQL, debugging, and unfamiliar schemas, with the judgment to catch output that looks right but isn't.
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

Data ingestion or CDC tooling: DataX, Sqoop, Debezium, Fivetran, or similar.
An OLAP / MPP engine: StarRocks, Doris, ClickHouse, Redshift, or similar.
Spark performance work: partitioning, shuffle, skew, and memory tuning.
AWS cost optimization: EMR instance sizing and Spot strategy, S3 lifecycle policies.
Lakehouse formats (Iceberg, Hudi, Delta), streaming (Kafka, Flink), dbt, or a data quality framework.
QuickSight or another BI tool: dataset and permission design.
Self-directed learning: a project, an open-source contribution, or a tool you picked up on your own and put to real use

Benefits

Salary Range:

$100,000 -120,000

Benefits:

Fully paid medical, dental, and vision insurance (partial coverage for dependents)
Contributions to 401k funds
Over four weeks of PTO per year
Bi-annual pay increases
Health and wellness benefits, including free gym membership
Quarterly team-building events

We believe that diversity fuels innovation, collaboration, and drives our entrepreneurial spirit. As a global company, we highly value diverse perspectives and are committed to cultivating an environment where all voices are heard, respected, and valued. If you share our passion and connection to this mission, we welcome you to apply and join us in building a vibrant and inclusive team at TP-Link Systems Inc.

The Opportunity

**At this time, Ally will not sponsor a new applicant for employment authorization for this position**

Location: Charlotte, NC in-office

We are seeking a hands-on Software Engineer to contribute to the design, development, testing, deployment, support, and continuous improvement of applications across the Audit and Risk technology portfolio. In this role, you will help deliver technology solutions that support assurance, testing and monitoring, risk management, and business resilience. You will work closely with engineers, product owners, business partners, and technology teams to develop high-quality solutions while supporting the stability and reliability of production applications.

The Work Itself

Contribute to the design, development, testing, debugging, implementation, and support of software solutions that deliver business value and improve operational efficiency.
Develop full-stack features using technologies such as TypeScript, JavaScript, React, Next.js, Node.js/Express, SQL, and Python.
Create and enhance RESTful APIs, including controllers, middleware, service layers, route handlers, and secure authentication and authorization capabilities.
Implement database enhancements including schema changes, migrations, indexing strategies, seed data, and query optimization. Experience with PostgreSQL or AWS Aurora is beneficial.

Participate in Agile ceremonies including sprint planning, backlog refinement, daily standups, sprint reviews, and retrospectives.
Contribute to DevOps and CI/CD practices that support reliable deployment, monitoring, and maintenance of applications.
Maintain software quality through unit testing, automated testing, code reviews, and adherence to engineering standards and best practices.
Support system integration testing and user acceptance testing activities by analyzing, troubleshooting, and resolving defects.
Participate in production readiness activities including deployments, changes, service account maintenance, documentation updates, vulnerability remediation, and operational support activities.
Troubleshoot application and user issues, perform root-cause analysis, communicate status and risks clearly, and coordinate with infrastructure, database, security, network, cloud, platform, identity and access management, and other technology teams to resolve issues.
Review security findings, vulnerability assessments, and penetration-test results and assist with remediation efforts in accordance with technology risk and compliance requirements.
Create and maintain technical documentation, deployment procedures, support runbooks, support guides, and knowledge base articles.
Collaborate effectively with engineers, architects, product owners, and business stakeholders to deliver solutions that meet business needs.
Participate in innovation activities, proof-of-concepts, hackathons, and continuous improvement efforts that help advance engineering practices and business capabilities.
Participate in scheduled after-hours work when required for production deployments, maintenance activities, or critical support events. Day-to-day work and support activities are primarily performed during business hours.
