1+ years of relevant software engineering experience.
Experience developing software through all phases of the software development lifecycle, including design, development, testing, deployment, support, and maintenance.
Proficiency with TypeScript and experience building applications using React or a comparable modern front-end framework.
Experience developing or supporting RESTful APIs using Node.js/Express or similar frameworks, including controllers, middleware, service layers, and authentication integration.
Experience working with relational databases, SQL, and scripting languages such as Python to support application development and data processing.
Experience with source control, testing, debugging, secure coding practices, code reviews, and modern software delivery practices.
Ability to troubleshoot application issues and support production systems through standard change, release, and support processes.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to create technical documentation and communicate effectively with engineers, technology partners, and business stakeholders.
Ability to work effectively in a collaborative Agile team environment and contribute to continuous improvement initiatives.
Experience supporting applications used by Internal Audit, Enterprise Risk, Compliance, Controls, or other regulated business functions is a plus.
Experience with cloud platforms such as AWS. AWS experience with services such as ECS Fargate, Aurora, RDS Proxy, API Gateway, IAM, Secrets Manager, or S3 is beneficial.
Experience supporting, configuring, integrating, or enhancing vendor-provided enterprise applications is beneficial.
Salesforce administration, configuration, or support experience is preferred. Apex development experience is not required.
Experience balancing feature delivery with application sustainment, user support, technical debt reduction, security remediation, and operational improvements.
Demonstrated curiosity, ownership, problem-solving ability, and willingness to learn new technologies and business domains.
Ability to work independently on well-defined assignments while collaborating with senior engineers and technical leads on more complex initiatives.

1+ years of experience
High school Diploma or GED equivalent

plan for the near and long term with an industry-leading 401K retirement savings plan with matching and company contributions, student loan pay downs and 529 educational save up assistance programs, tuition reimbursement, employee stock purchase plan, and financial learning center and financial coach access.

flexible health and insurance options including medical, dental and vision, employee, spouse and child life insurance, short- and long-term disability, pre-tax Health Savings Account with employer contributions, Healthcare FSA, critical illness, accident & hospital indemnity insurance, and a total well-being program that helps you and your family stay on track physically, socially, emotionally, and financially.

other benefits including Mentally Fit Employee Assistance Program, subsidized and discounted Weight Watchers® program and other employee discount programs.

Job Description

The Solomon and Keller laboratories in Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences at Stanford University are seeking a joint Software Developer Associate to develop software for the storage, management, access, and analysis of human electrophysiological data. The role will also be expected to contribute to existing software packages for conducting brain stimulation experiments.

The goal of both labs is to understand the fundamental principles governing how the human brain responds to electrical stimulation, and to develop next-generation neurotherapeutics to treat neuropsychiatric conditions. The Software Developer Associate will assist in this mission by developing software that enables research analysts to efficiently and flexibly interact with complex human neural data and associated metadata (including neuroimaging, behavioral, medical, and audio-visual measures). The Associate will work under the general supervision of the laboratory PI and in direct collaboration with postdoctoral researchers and graduate students.

Assessment of users needs relating to the flexible access and analysis of human electrophysiology data and associated research metadata.
Assist in the development of new Python-based software packages and APIs to enable easy, efficient, and fast analysis of these data.

Contribute to refinements of existing software packages for conducting transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) research experiments, including hardware/software interfacing and GUI development.

new_jobs.title: Software Engineer, Infrastructure
new_jobs.description:
About Niantic Spatial

AI has learned from almost everything online, but it still struggles with the physical world, where 99.5% of economic activity happens. It doesn’t know where things are, how spaces fit together, or what changes over time.

That’s one of the biggest unsolved problems in AI, and it’s the one we’re solving at Niantic Spatial. We build spatial AI models and services so people and machines can reason, learn and act safely in the physical world. We turn camera imagery, video, sensor data and archives into accurate, AI-readable representations of real places that robots can train in and machines can use to know exactly where they are.

In physical AI, mistakes have real consequences. That’s why we build AI grounded in measured reality, not guesswork, so the people and machines relying on it can trust it to get things right.

Our team built some of the world’s most widely used maps. Now we’re building something bigger: a living, measured record of the real world that machines can query, learn from and use to understand how places change over time. If you want to help AI understand the world we actually live in, come build with us.

About The Role

You’ll join a small infrastructure team with broad, shared ownership — the engineers who keep Niantic Spatial running. The team covers the cloud platform, the developer tooling every engineer depends on, and the edge services our customers’ requests pass through. You’ll work across SRE, infrastructure, and developer platform alongside teammates who know the stack well, and you’ll grow into owning parts of it yourself. Because every engineer here builds on what this team provides, your work will also shape how the whole engineering org builds, ships, and operates.

What You'll Do

Cloud and SRE: Build and maintain cloud infrastructure as code, and help improve reliability through monitoring, alerting, and service-level objectives.
Developer Platform: Help run our source control, CI/CD pipelines, and build infrastructure so engineers can ship quickly and safely.
Production Operations: Share on-call, take part in incident response and follow-up, and automate away repetitive operational work.
Edge and Delivery: Help run the edge API gateway, CDN, and authentication and authorization systems with the rest of the team.
Compute and GPU Management: Help provision and monitor compute and GPU capacity across teams.
AI-Assisted Operations: Use AI tools to help build, automate, and maintain our infrastructure, and help shape how the team uses them.

What You'll Bring

Years of Experience: 3+ years in infrastructure, SRE, DevOps, or platform engineering.
Education: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
Infrastructure as Code: Experience managing infrastructure as code with tools such as Terraform, Pulumi, or similar.
Cloud: Hands-on experience with GCP, AWS, or another major cloud provider in production.
CI/CD: Experience building and maintaining CI/CD pipelines in GitLab, GitHub Actions, or similar.
Containers: Production experience with containers and container orchestration, such as Kubernetes.
Core Technical Skills: Proficiency in at least one programming language such as Python, Go, TypeScript, or C++, plus shell scripting and Linux systems.
AI in Your Workflow: Comfort using AI-assisted tools in your engineering work, or a strong interest in building that habit. We’ll help you ramp up on how we use AI here.

Nice to Have

Familiarity with API gateways, load balancers, or CDNs.
Familiarity with modern authentication and authorization, such as OAuth 2.0, OIDC, or cloud IAM.
Experience with GPU workloads or ML infrastructure.
Experience with message queuing systems.

Location & Work Model

This role is based in our San Francisco or Sunnyvale, CA office, or in Bellevue, WA. We work in a high-collaboration environment and ask team members to be on-site a minimum of 3 days per week.

Compensation & Benefits

The base salary range for this position is $171,000 - $230,000 for Bay Area candidates and $162,500 - $218,500 for Seattle/Bellevue candidates. Actual salary is based on assessed skills, experience, and location. This role is also eligible for equity, bonus, and benefits. Your recruiter can answer questions about total compensation during the hiring process.

We know the strongest candidates don't always tick every box. If you're excited about this role and believe you could do it well, we encourage you to apply even if your experience doesn't match every qualification listed — you may be exactly who we're looking for.

new_jobs.title: EGSE/Avionics Test Software Engineer
new_jobs.description:
Quantum Space is redefining mobility and maneuverability in space. Our high-mobility spacecraft platforms support national security, civil, and commercial missions with unmatched flexibility and propulsion capability. We build fast and iterate quickly.

Who We’re Looking For

We are seeking a technically driven EGSE/ Avionics Test Software Engineer to develop automated test software, Electrical Ground Support Equipment (EGSE) software, and hardware/software integration test infrastructure for spacecraft avionics supporting Ranger missions.

In this role, you will develop reusable test applications, instrument interfaces, and automated test sequencing capabilities used to verify spacecraft avionics hardware and software. You will work closely with avionics, flight software, electrical, systems, and test engineers to build reliable test infrastructure, troubleshoot complex hardware/software interactions, and ensure test results are accurate, repeatable, and defensible.

This position is ideal for an engineer who enjoys working at the intersection of software and hardware, solving difficult integration problems, and building robust test systems that directly contribute to flight readiness and mission success.

Where You’ll Make an Impact

Develop automated test software and EGSE software supporting spacecraft avionics development and verification
Design and develop reusable test applications, instrument interfaces, device drivers, test sequencing capabilities, and data acquisition tools
Develop software to control laboratory instrumentation and communicate with embedded avionics hardware
Build maintainable and extensible test frameworks that separate hardware interfaces, test logic, configuration, and data handling
Develop requirements-based verification tests, including positive and negative testing, boundary conditions, failure scenarios, and fault injection
Support hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) and hardware/software integration testing of spacecraft avionics
Develop automated functional and performance tests for flight computers and other avionics hardware
Troubleshoot complex hardware, firmware, software, communication interface, and test equipment issues using systematic root-cause analysis
Verify and validate automated test software and test equipment to ensure accurate and reliable results
Implement test logging and data collection practices that provide traceability and reproducibility across hardware and software configurations
Collaborate with avionics, flight software, systems, electrical, and test teams to develop verification approaches and resolve integration issues
Participate in code reviews and contribute to software development, configuration management, and continuous integration practices
Operate within a fast-paced development environment focused on rapid execution, technical excellence, and mission success

What It Takes

Bachelor's, Master's, or Ph.D. in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, Aerospace Engineering, or a related technical discipline
Experience developing automated test software using LabVIEW, Python, C/C++, or equivalent programming environments
Experience developing software that controls laboratory instrumentation and communicates with embedded hardware
Experience developing reusable and maintainable automated test applications, frameworks, or test infrastructure
Experience troubleshooting and diagnosing complex hardware/software integration issues
Understanding of software verification principles, including requirements-based testing, boundary conditions, negative testing, and fault injection
Experience verifying that automated test software and test equipment are operating correctly and producing reliable results
Familiarity with software configuration management and version control tools such as Git
Strong software debugging, analytical, and problem-solving skills

Nice-to-Have Experience

Experience developing automated test systems or EGSE for spacecraft, aerospace, defense, or other complex embedded systems
Experience developing test frameworks with modular device drivers, reusable interfaces, automated test sequencing, logging, assertions, and configuration management
Experience communicating with hardware over interfaces such as Ethernet, TCP/UDP, RS-422/485, SpaceWire, SPI, I2C, or similar protocols
Experience testing asynchronous hardware and developing software that accounts for timing, synchronization, timeouts, and communication errors
Experience with hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) testing and simulation environments
Experience developing automated power-on, functional, or acceptance testing for flight computers or other avionics hardware
Experience with automated fault injection and verification of fault detection, isolation, and recovery behavior
Experience using laboratory instrumentation, protocol analyzers, data acquisition systems, or similar test equipment
Experience developing unit tests, simulated instrument interfaces, or other methods for validating automated test software
Experience with CI/CD pipelines, automated builds, automated testing, code reviews, and software configuration management
Understanding of embedded firmware and flight software architectures
Experience working with spacecraft avionics or flight hardware
Experience supporting fast-paced aerospace, defense, or commercial space programs

What You’ll Get

Ownership – Take responsibility for automated test software and infrastructure that directly supports the development and verification of mission-critical spacecraft avionics
Innovation – Build robust test frameworks and automation capabilities that accelerate spacecraft development and improve verification efficiency
Impact – Help ensure spacecraft avionics and flight systems perform reliably through rigorous, repeatable, and defensible testing
Growth – Work across avionics, flight software, electrical, systems, and test engineering while expanding your expertise in spacecraft hardware/software integration
Compensation – Competitive salary, equity, and comprehensive benefits including medical, dental, vision, generous leave, HSA, 401(k) matching, and equity participation

Location:
Rockville, MD or Hawthorne, CA

Base Salary:
$110,000 to $160,000

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Quantum Space's total compensation package.

Additional Requirements

To comply with U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including ITAR, applicants must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident, protected individual per 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.

new_jobs.title: Machine Learning Engineer, Growth Platform
new_jobs.description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About The Team

Growth Platform builds the machine learning systems that help businesses discover and use the Stripe products that meet their needs. Our recommendations reach users across the Dashboard, email, onboarding, documentation, and AI agent interfaces. We combine an understanding of each business with models that decide which recommendation is useful, when to show it, and how to learn from the outcome.

Our work spans recommendation and ranking models, contextual bandits, agent-based recommendations, and the data and evaluation systems behind them. We build shared capabilities that product, marketing, and sales teams can use across Stripe. Success means helping businesses take useful actions and adopt products that help them grow, while keeping recommendations relevant and avoiding unnecessary messages.

What you’ll do

You will build and operate production ML systems that improve how Stripe recommends products, content, and next steps to businesses. You will own work from problem definition and feature development through training, evaluation, deployment, monitoring, and iteration. Working with data scientists, engineers, and product partners, you will turn model improvements into measurable user and business outcomes.

Responsibilities

Design, train, evaluate, deploy, and maintain models for recommendation, ranking, and personalized action selection across Growth Platform surfaces.
Improve contextual bandit and policy-learning approaches, including exploration, reward design, and how recommendations adapt to user context and feedback.
Build agent-based recommendation capabilities that use business context to identify relevant products and integration options, with evaluations that test recommendation quality and usefulness.
Develop reliable data and feature pipelines for training and inference. Improve data freshness, feature quality, and consistency between training and production.
Build reusable tooling for model evaluation, retraining, and safe rollout so the team can test and ship improvements faster.
Own the quality and operation of the team's ML components: write tested production code, monitor models and pipelines, investigate failures, and improve reliability, latency, and cost.
Design and analyze online experiments with data science partners. Connect offline evaluation to product adoption and incremental impact, with guardrails for dismissals, unsubscribes, and user experience.
Partner with product engineering to integrate models into recommendation delivery systems, and with ML infrastructure teams to use and improve Stripe's shared training, feature, and serving capabilities.
Work with product, marketing, and sales partners to identify problems that shared ML capabilities can solve, and make practical choices about where modeling adds value.

Who you are

You are a machine learning engineer with a builder mindset. You care about the business problem, the quality of the model, and what happens after it ships. You can move between modeling and software engineering, make practical tradeoffs, and take ownership of an ambiguous problem through production and measurement.

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum Requirements

3+ years of industry experience in machine learning engineering, software engineering, or applied data science, with hands-on experience building and shipping ML models in production.
Strong programming skills in Python and experience writing maintainable, tested production code.
Practical experience designing, training, and evaluating ML models using frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, XGBoost, or scikit-learn.
Experience building data or feature pipelines, proficiency in SQL, and familiarity with distributed data processing tools such as Spark or PySpark.
A strong understanding of statistics, model evaluation, and experimentation, including the ability to recognize data leakage and distinguish offline model improvements from business impact.
Experience deploying, monitoring, and debugging production ML systems, and evaluating tradeoffs among model quality, reliability, latency, and cost.
Ability to turn an open-ended business problem into a technical approach and collaborate effectively with engineering, data science, product, and business partners.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with recommendation systems, ranking, personalization, or marketplace and advertising optimization.
Experience with contextual bandits, policy learning, causal inference, or off-policy evaluation.
Experience building and evaluating LLM applications, including structured extraction, embeddings, or recommendations grounded in user and business context.
Experience building reusable ML capabilities used by multiple products or teams, including training automation, feature systems, or model monitoring.
Experience with product growth, lifecycle messaging, or systems that balance short-term engagement with longer-term user outcomes.

Hybrid work at Stripe

This role is available either in an office or a remote location (35+ miles or 56+ km from a Stripe office).

In-office expectations

Office-assigned Stripes spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. This hits a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility about how to do this in a way that makes sense for individuals and their teams.

Working remotely at Stripe

A remote location is defined as being 35 miles (56 kilometers) or more from one of our offices. While you would be welcome to come into the office for team/business meetings, on-sites, meet-ups, and events, our expectation is you would regularly work from home rather than a Stripe office. Stripe does not cover the cost of relocating to a remote location. We encourage you to apply for roles that match the location where you currently live or plan to live.

Pay and benefits

The annual US base salary range for this role is $180,000 - $270,000. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. This salary range may be inclusive of several career levels at Stripe and will be narrowed during the interview process based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and location. Applicants interested in this role and who are not located in the US may request the annual salary range for their location during the interview process.

Additional benefits for this role may include: equity, company bonus or sales commissions/bonuses; 401(k) plan; medical, dental, and vision benefits; and wellness stipends.

We look forward to hearing from you.

At Stripe, we're looking for people with passion, grit, and integrity. You're encouraged to apply even if your experience doesn't precisely match the job description. Your skills and passion will stand out—and set you apart—especially if your career has taken some extraordinary twists and turns. At Stripe, we welcome diverse perspectives and people who think rigorously and aren't afraid to challenge assumptions. Join us.

Apply now

This role is first and foremost about engineering excellence: strong fundamentals, clean architecture, and the ability to ship end-to-end features across the stack.

We're looking for someone who treats AI coding assistants as a core part of the craft, not a side skill — using tools like Cursor, Claude Code, and Codex daily to move faster, explore designs, and raise code quality.

Own features through the full lifecycle: solution design, development, testing, deployment, and production support.

You're Our Person If...

Proficiency in modern frontend technologies (JavaScript/TypeScript, HTML, CSS, modern frameworks) and backend development (object-oriented programming, RESTful API design, databases/SQL, data modeling).
Hands-on, daily experience using AI-assisted coding tools such as Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, or similar — able to write precise prompts and critically evaluate AI-generated code for correctness, security, and performance.

A true engineer at heart: someone who can reason about architecture, write clean code, and diagnose hard bugs — with or without AI in the loop.
Genuinely AI-native: you reach for Cursor, Claude Code, or Codex by default, and use them to build fluency across the stack, not just in your specialty.
Curious and adaptable — comfortable picking up new platforms (including Salesforce, Mulesoft) quickly when the work calls for it.
Ownership mindset: you drive features to done, care about quality, and elevate the engineers around you.
Excited about applying AI meaningfully to real business problems — automation, decision support, and smarter workflows .

Unleash Your Potential

When you join Salesforce, you’ll be limitless in all areas of your life. Our benefits and resources support you to find balance and be your best , and our AI agents accelerate your impact so you can do your best . Together, we’ll bring the power of Agentforce to organizations of all sizes and deliver amazing experiences that customers love. Apply today to not only shape the future — but to redefine what’s possible — for yourself, for AI, and the world.

new_jobs.description:

Careers that change lives start here. Medtronic is a global leader in healthcare technology with a Mission to alleviate pain, restore health, and extend life. Our 95,000 employees work across more than 150 countries to put patients first — developing innovative medical technologies that improve the lives of 72+ million patients each year. Your unique talents will help shape the future of healthcare while building a career grounded in purpose, growth, and impact.

A Day in the Life

At Medtronic, we bring bold ideas forward with speed and decisiveness to put patients first in everything we do. In-person exchanges are invaluable to our work. We’re working a minimum of 4 days a week onsite as part of our commitment to fostering a culture of professional growth and cross-functional collaboration as we work together to engineer the extraordinary.

As a Software Engineer – UI/UX (Qt/QML) You will own significant features and workflows in the Prism Mapping application UI — the surfaces clinicians use during procedures and case review. A typical week mixes deep Qt/QML and C++/Python implementation, partnership with UX designers translating Figma designs into responsive production interfaces, integration work with the visualization, signals, and infrastructure teams, and the kind of debugging that happens when application state, real-time data, and human interaction all collide. You'll make architecture decisions about UI state, data binding, and interaction patterns; mentor newer UI engineers; and set the standard for what a high-quality, clinically-safe interface looks like in our product.

About The Affera Prism Mapping System

The Affera Prism Mapping System is an advanced electrophysiology mapping platform used by physicians to diagnose and guide the treatment of cardiac arrhythmias. It captures and processes signals from inside the beating heart, builds detailed real-time three-dimensional maps of cardiac anatomy and electrical activity, and presents that information to clinicians and mapping specialists during live procedures. Engineers on this team build the software that makes that possible — from the runtime and data pipelines that move signals in milliseconds, to the algorithms that turn raw signals into clinically meaningful information, to the visualization and UI surfaces clinicians rely on in the lab.

Primary Responsibilities

Own significant UI features and clinical workflows in Qt/QML.

About Pallet

Pallet is building AI Agents to transform the physical economy, a $12 trillion global TAM. We've raised $50M from top investors, including General Catalyst, Bessemer Venture Partners, and Bain Capital Ventures.

Our mission is to increase the efficiency of the global supply chain by automating the manual workflows that slow supply chain teams down. Our flagship platform provides end-to-end visibility, and control.

As companies across the physical economy look to drive efficiency, many are turning to Pallet to lead the way. With deep supply chain expertise and cutting-edge AI capabilities, we're positioned to build the next $10B company powering the physical economy.

Join us and work alongside leaders from Google, DoorDash, YC, and more to shape the future of supply chain technology.

About The Role

We're hiring a Software Engineer, Agent Delivery to deploy production AI agents inside some of the world's largest supply chain companies.

You'll work directly with customer operators, engineers, and executives to understand how critical workflows actually run. Then you'll design integrations, debug production systems, and ship AI-powered workflows into environments that are often undocumented, fragmented, and business-critical.

This role sits at the intersection of engineering, product, and customer operations. You'll own deployments from initial discovery through production launch, spending time with customers both remotely and onsite, solving complex operational problems and turning those solutions into reusable product capabilities.

Success in this role is measured by outcomes: can you get systems live, make them reliable, and solve problems in environments you don't fully control? Every deployment teaches us something new about how supply chain companies operate. The patterns you uncover become product features, and what you solve for one customer often becomes a capability we ship across the platform.

The impact you will have

Lead high-impact customer deployments from problem definition through production, designing, prototyping, building, and deploying AI agents and workflows that change how work gets done and run reliably at scale.
Embed in customer workflows and build relationships from ICs and operators up to executives, turning messy business requirements into clear technical solutions that solve the underlying problem, not just the first request.
Make design decisions across agent behavior, application logic, data, evals, security, and reliability, and set the patterns for how Pallet agents are deployed in production.
Connect Pallet agents to the systems, APIs, and data customers already rely on, working directly with their engineering and ops teams to get around technical constraints.
Stay accountable after launch by debugging failures, evaluating and improving agent quality, and working with Engineering and Product to clear anything blocking a successful deployment.
Turn what you learn in the field into reusable agents, integrations, evals, and frameworks, and bring recurring needs and product gaps back to Product and Engineering to shape the core platform.

Who You Are

1+ years of experience building and owning production systems in high-growth startups or similarly demanding environments.
Strong experience working with APIs, integrations, authentication systems, and event-driven architectures.
Proven ability to debug complex systems in production.
Comfortable operating in ambiguous environments where documentation is incomplete, and requirements evolve quickly.
Strong communication skills and the ability to build trust with technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Experience working directly with customers is a strong plus

Our Tech Stack

Backend: Node + TypeScript on Encore.dev. Event-driven design with message passing and queues. Hosted on GCP
Database: PostgreSQL
LLMs: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google for foundation models; fine-tuned models on Vertex AI
Browser Automation: Playwright
Frontend: Next.js + React + TypeScript. Hosted on Vercel
Observability: Datadog for logging and metrics

Location:
San Francisco, Fidi 5 days a week

Final compensation will be determined based on a combination of factors, including experience, qualifications, and location.

new_jobs.description:
GM Performance Power Units - Concord, NC

Data Engineer - Onsite

Job Summary

Build and operate reliable data pipelines for power unit test and performance activities, using AWS as the primary cloud environment. Make engineering data accessible, traceable and ready for analysis, while retaining the context needed to interpret results correctly.

Work with Test, Performance, Controls and IT teams to turn files, measurements and test events into supported data products. Collaborate with the business and manufacturing data role to connect test results with approved engine, build and component information in Microsoft Fabric.

Key Responsibilities

Build and maintain ingestion pipelines for agreed dyno, test rig, instrumentation and performance sources. Support batch, file and streaming patterns where requirements justify them.
Preserve source files and relevant timestamps, units, calibration references, run identifiers and acquisition context. Implement validation and make missing or disputed context visible.
Develop documented datasets and processing pipelines using Python and SQL. Implement duplicate prevention, late-data handling, checkpoints and controlled replay.
Link test runs to approved engine, build and serialize component identities. Work with system owners to resolve mismatches and maintain traceable mappings.
Prepare and publish agreed test and performance summaries from the AWS environment for use by the business and manufacturing data platform. Work with the business & manufacturing data engineer to establish controlled data exchanges, including the reference data needed to link test results to engines, builds and components.
Monitor data freshness, pipeline failures, processing performance and cloud consumption. Tune storage, retention and compute against agreed engineering and cost requirements.
Use source control, peer review, automated checks and controlled deployment. Maintain separate development and production configurations and protect credentials.
Document pipelines, dependencies and recovery procedures. Train a nominated deputy and contribute to an agreed support and incident response model.

Required Qualifications

Practical experience building and supporting production data pipelines on AWS, including S3 and appropriate processing, orchestration and monitoring services.
Strong Python and SQL skills, with experience handling large files, time-series data or other complex engineering datasets.
Understanding of incremental processing, idempotency, schema changes, data quality controls and recovery from partial failure.
Experience with Git, code review, testing and repeatable deployments. Ability to work with infrastructure as code and CI/CD practices.
Understanding of cloud access controls, service identities, encryption and secure connectivity, working with infrastructure and security specialists.
Ability to diagnose failures, explain cost drivers and document a service so another engineer can maintain it.
Ability to translate engineering requirements into clear data contracts and acceptance tests, and communicate effectively with technical and business colleagues.
Relevant qualification or equivalent practical experience. Candidates should demonstrate delivered outcomes rather than a specific certification alone.

Preferred Qualifications

Automotive, motorsport, aerospace, manufacturing or another test-intensive engineering environment.
Dyno or rig data, signal alignment, timestamp synchronization, calibration context, telemetry formats and engineering metadata.
Parquet or Delta Lake, distributed processing, and AWS services such as Glue, Athena, EMR, Kinesis or equivalent tools selected for the workload.
Cross-cloud data exchange, Microsoft Fabric or Power BI integration, and linking test results to PLM, ERP or lifing records.
Databricks on AWS where justified by the processing requirements. Databricks experience is beneficial rather than a prerequisite.

Why Join Us

Ready to be part of a team that pushes boundaries both on and off the track? At GM Performance Power Units, we are developing a new era of performance for the Formula 1 grid. Joining us means entering a startup racing environment backed by a legacy of engineering excellence, giving you the rare opportunity to help build a world-class program from day one. We believe in rewarding innovation and powering potential. As part of our team, you’ll benefit from a competitive and comprehensive package designed to support your performance, well-being, and future, helping you thrive at every level.

It’s all part of our commitment to creating a workplace that’s as high-performing and forward-thinking as the people who make it succeed.

Join Us And Help Power What’s Next.

You’ll play a pivotal role in ensuring the reliability and performance of a next-generation Formula 1 power unit. Our culture rewards precision, innovation, and the relentless pursuit of performance.

new_jobs.title: Sr. Software Engineer - Backend/Full-stack
new_jobs.description:
Instrumental builds the manufacturing acceleration platform behind the world's most complex electronics. We capture digital exhaust and engineering context from assembly lines — images, test logs, BOM data, performance, repair cycles — and our AI engines identify insights that are difficult or impossible for human engineers to find. We accelerate the companies building the AI era by improving manufacturing yield, throughput, and ramp. NVIDIA, Meta, L3Harris, and their manufacturing partners rely on Instrumental to accelerate new product introduction and production.

We're entering one of the most important periods in our company's history. Over the next year, we'll be rebuilding our platform layer for a scale it wasn't originally built for — and the engineer who joins now will shape that architecture as much as anyone.

We're looking for a Backend/Platform engineer who owns hard, ambiguous systems problems end-to-end, and who does it in a way that makes the rest of engineering want to build on what you ship. This isn't a role where you inherit an architecture and maintain it. You'll partner directly with engineering leadership and teams across product, AI, and edge systems — not just to keep the platform running, but to raise the bar on how we build.

What You'll Be Doing

Own the systems that matter most. Take full lifecycle ownership of core platform services — design, build, deploy, operate — especially the ones where the obvious architecture doesn't hold up, and you have to design a better one.
Make the rest of engineering better at shipping. You'll push back when a design won't scale, an approach trades short-term speed for long-term pain, or a "good enough" isn't. You earn the standing to do this by being right, consistently, and by being someone teams want in the room.
Move fast without creating friction. You'll make architectural calls, iterate in real time, and adjust course mid-build — all while keeping other teams, and the systems they depend on, aligned and stable. No surprises, no silent breakage.
Build the platform as you go. Better tooling, smarter use of AI-assisted development, sharper observability and incident response — you'll leave the platform meaningfully stronger than you found it, and you'll do it in a way that earns trust rather than working around people.

This role probably isn't the right fit if...

You want a well-defined system to maintain, rather than one to build and rebuild as the business scales.
When something breaks or doesn't scale, you wait for direction instead of diagnosing and fixing it yourself.
You've mostly worked in codebases where the hard architectural decisions were already made — this job is proactive, not maintenance.
You measure success by "it shipped" rather than "it shipped, it holds up, and the team trusts how we got there."
You've built a reputation for moving fast at the cost of the people around you — trust and speed both matter here, not one traded for the other.

Requirements

5+ years as a software engineer, with real ownership of production systems at a startup — you've designed and shipped systems end to end, not just contributed to systems someone else architected.
Fluency in Python or Go, with strong data modeling and system design instincts.
Experience building SaaS or multi-tenant systems, and the product judgment that comes with it.
A track record of solving hard, ambiguous engineering problems — untangling messy domains, making design decisions with incomplete information, and owning the outcome — not just building well-scoped features.
Fluent in AI-assisted development as a default way of working, and able to bring others along on it.
Evidence that other engineers and leaders trusted your judgment and wanted you on their hardest problems — examples that speak to this are a plus.

We’re a growing team that works collaboratively, supports each other, and is energized by having an impact. We value passion and the ability to learn — you’re encouraged to apply even if your experience doesn’t match the job description precisely!

The following is a representative annual base salary range for this position within the Bay Area: $170,000-$221,000. In addition, job level and salary opportunities are evaluated during our interview process — we review each applicant's experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities.

Instrumental is proud to offer a highly-rated variety of benefits, including health, vision, dental, commuter plans, and parental leave.

new_jobs.description:
Description

Financial systems must keep working, even as the technology behind them changes.

As an IT Application Developer with the Department of Social and Health Services (DSHS), you'll update financial applications to support Washington's One Washington initiative and the transition to Workday. These systems support accounting, budgeting, and financial operations that help DSHS serve Washington residents.

You won't be expected to learn these systems alone.

You'll work alongside senior developers to understand requirements, design solutions, write code, and test changes. Your week will include Agile development cycles, troubleshooting, peer reviews, and collaboration with business and technical teams.

We encourage you to apply if
you enjoy solving technical problems, can explain your design decisions, and welcome feedback. You understand that reliable software depends on both sound code and a clear understanding of business needs.

Your first 90 days
are about learning the applications, development tools, and business processes. You'll review existing code, work with senior developers, and begin contributing changes.

Within your first year, success means you can develop, test, and implement changes that support the One Washington transition.

The opportunity comes with a defined timeline.

There are two one-year project positions, with possible extensions dependent on additional funding. You'll work Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., with at least two days each week at Office Building 2 during your first three months. No additional travel is expected. The Olympia area offers access to South Puget Sound, parks, and trails, although wet winters and commuting conditions are worth considering.

Still reading? Here's what you'll do.

Some Of What You'll Do

Develop and maintain financial applications and data interfaces.
Analyze requirements and design technical solutions.
Write, test, debug, and review application code.
Update systems and integrations for One Washington and Workday.
Troubleshoot production issues and application failures.
Participate in Agile development cycles and peer reviews.
Collaborate with senior developers and business teams.
Document system changes, designs, and test procedures.
Follow development, security, and quality standards.

Who Should Apply

Meet one of these pathways:

Seven years of recent professional software development and maintenance experience; or
An associate degree in computer science or a closely related field and five years of professional software development and maintenance experience; or
A bachelor's degree or higher in computer science or a closely related field and three years of professional software development and maintenance experience.

Qualifying experience includes analyzing, designing, implementing, programming, or maintaining software applications.

You must also have experience or training in some of these technologies: Java, C#, .NET, Microsoft SQL Server, Transact-SQL, HTML, CSS, or JavaScript.

Preferred Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Experience with C#, .NET, JavaScript, SQL Server, or Transact-SQL.
Knowledge of SQL Server Reporting Services (SSRS) or Integration Services (SSIS).
Experience with TFS, Azure DevOps, or Agile/Scrum.
Experience with application integration and production troubleshooting.
Ability to explain technical decisions and collaborate during reviews.

Submit

How to Apply

Your resume.
Your cover letter.
Three professional references.

Include details about the applications you've developed, technologies used, and your contributions.

Questions?

Email recruiter Kris George at kris.george@dshs.wa.gov and reference job number 08822.

Xcelerate Solutions is seeking an Artifact Management and Secure Software Development Specialist SME Software Engineer for this effort will be responsible for providing guidance and targeted assistance in migrating NCIS Mission Applications to a secure software development toolchain and ensuring compliance with DON-CIO policies regarding secure software development practices and products.

TS/SCI

Key Responsibilities:

Design, develop, implement, and maintain secure, scalable, full-stack software applications supporting mission-critical enterprise systems, with a focus on Secure Development Operations (SecDevOps) principles.
Develop and maintain software applications using compiled and interpreted programming languages while ensuring compliance with secure coding standards and enterprise security requirements.
Design, develop, and optimize relational and NoSQL database solutions to support application functionality, performance, data integrity, and security.
Establish, implement, and enforce secure coding standards, including code quality, Zero Trust security principles, Software Bill of Materials (SBOM), and secure dependency management.
Configure, administer, and maintain software artifact management repositories using Nexus, JFrog Artifactory, NuGet, or comparable technologies to ensure secure storage, version control, and distribution of software components.
Implement and maintain Static Application Security Testing (SAST), Dynamic Application Security Testing (DAST), and code quality tools, including SonarQube, Aikido, CodeQL, or equivalent platforms, based on their supported capabilities.
Integrate automated security scanning, code quality assessments, vulnerability detection, and dependency analysis into CI/CD pipelines to strengthen application security throughout the software development lifecycle.
Establish and enforce Git-based source control practices, including pre-commit hooks, branch protection policies, pull request reviews, and automated code validation.
Implement secure software supply chain practices to ensure software dependencies, third-party libraries, and application artifacts meet organizational security and compliance requirements.
Identify, assess, prioritize, and remediate software vulnerabilities, insecure dependencies, and code quality issues to reduce security risks across enterprise applications.
Collaborate with DevSecOps engineers, cybersecurity personnel, infrastructure teams, and Mission Application developers to implement consistent security controls and secure development practices.
Provide technical guidance and mentorship to Mission Application developers on secure coding methodologies, application security, vulnerability remediation, and compliance requirements.
Apply software engineering and security principles across diverse programming languages, operating systems, development frameworks, and hosting environments.
Evaluate and implement emerging technologies, security tools, and development methodologies to address evolving mission requirements and improve software engineering capabilities.
Support security assessments, accreditation activities, and compliance reviews by maintaining software security documentation, SBOM records, vulnerability reports, and evidence of implemented security controls.
Develop and maintain secure software development procedures, technical documentation, coding standards, and best practices to support consistent implementation across the enterprise.
Promote a culture of security awareness, accountability, and continuous compliance by establishing repeatable processes and encouraging sustained adoption of secure software development standards.

Minimum Requirements:

High School with 10+ years (or commensurate experience)
Clearance Required: Top Secret/SCI
Expertise in Secure Software Development (SecDevOps focus) across a full-stack domain, including database (relational and NoSQL) and application development (compiled and interpreted languages)
Expertise in secure coding practices (including code quality, Zero Trust, SBOM, and secure dependency management)
Expertise with artifact management toolsets (Nexus, Artifactory, NuGet, etc) and SAST/DAST code quality platforms (SonarQube, Aikido, CodeQL, or similar) and Git-oriented supporting capabilities (such as pre-commit hooks and branch management rules)
Must be comfortable applying software engineering principles to disparate languages, operating systems, and hosting environments holistically, learning new technologies as needed to support emergent mission needs, and providing guidance to Mission Application developers to build a culture of compliance regarding sustained implementation of such objectives. Shares overlap/redundancy with other two SME software developer positions.
IAT II Certification

new_jobs.title: Software Engineer, Growth
new_jobs.description:
About Suno

We're building the world's first creative entertainment platform, where the entire world can feel the joy and fulfillment of making music. Music is for everyone: Our users include everyone from grandmothers creating songs for their loved ones, to Grammy winners using Suno Studio, our power tool, to make the most popular hits in the world.

Building the future of entertainment requires ambition. The pace is fast, the problems are hard, and the work demands ownership and intensity. For the right people, it’s incredibly rewarding: a chance to shape a new medium, work with a small team that cares deeply about quality, make music, drink too much coffee, and build something that millions of people use to express themselves in ways that were never before possible.

Suno is the fastest growing consumer entertainment company and the leader in AI music. We are backed by leading investors including Bond Capital, Menlo Ventures, Lightspeed Venture Partners, IVP, Forerunner, Union Square Ventures, Alkeon, Quiet, Matrix Partners, Schroders Capital and, NVentures (venture arm of NVIDIA).

About The Role

Growth Engineering at Suno owns the path from "someone hears about Suno" to "someone who creates music, comes back, and subscribes." That includes onboarding, paywalls and pricing, credits and billing, lifecycle messaging, logged-out surfaces and SEO, and the attribution and experimentation systems underneath all of it. Millions of people hit these surfaces every day.

You'll work on a team of web, iOS, and Android engineers. The team runs on experiments: you'll form a hypothesis, ship the test, read the result, and either scale it or retire it. Most projects have a small lean team on them.

We're a small team inside a company that is still moving fast. You'll have a say in what gets prioritized, and work directly with PMs, designers, data scientists, and marketers to deliver results for Suno.

Check out our Suno version of the job here: https://suno.com/s/fgke9OYJlf54RMKs

What You’ll Do

Own user growth or revenue projects end-to-end: from identifying opportunities through shipping and measuring results.
Partner closely with product, marketing, and design to translate their goals into a prioritized plan, ship fast, and measure impact with data.
Build and iterate across the full stack: frontend, backend, and data analysis.
Design and run experiments, working with product and data science on instrumentation, measurement, and result interpretation.
Create scalable and performant infrastructure that support growth campaigns and initiatives.

What You’ll Need

5+ years of software engineering experience, or equivalent demonstrated expertise.
Experience shipping full-stack web features to production.
History of owning outcomes rather than tickets: projects where you chose what to build, shipped it, and can say what happened to the metric afterward.
Comfort with data: asking critical questions about data, running queries on it, isolating signal from noise, and reading out results
A bias toward shipping fast without sacrificing code quality or user experience, and the judgment to decide when to optimize for what.
Genuine interest in music, and in the people making it with Suno.

Nice to have

Experience in at least one of our core areas: consumer growth and experimentation, subscriptions and monetization, or marketing engineering (SEO/AEO, CRO, CMS, attribution, lifecycle/CRM).
Cross-platform experience shipping features on web and mobile.

Additional Notes:
Applicants must be eligible to work in the US.

Location:
This is an onsite role in our Chelsea, NYC office.

Perks & Benefits For Full-Time Employees

Company Equity Package
401(k) with 3% Employer Match & Roth 401(k)
Medical, Dental, & Vision Insurance (PPO w/ HSA & FSA options)
11 Paid Holidays + Unlimited PTO & Sick Time
16 Weeks of Paid Parental Leave
Creative Education Stipend
Generous Commuter Allowance
In-Office Lunch (5 days per week)

new_jobs.title: Platform Engineer
new_jobs.description:
MANTECH
seeks a motivated, career and customer-oriented Platform Engineer
to join our team in Chantilly, VA
.

The Platform Engineer will support mission-critical data operations by designing, building, and optimizing large-scale data ingest and processing solutions in a Big Data environment. In this role, you will enable reliable, performant Elastic clusters and data pipelines that support analytic and operational needs across the full data lifecycle. You will own the Elasticsearch cluster lifecycle, build and maintain GitLab and Jenkins CI/CD pipelines, support enterprise RHEL hardware, and lead innovative efforts to integrate next-generation technologies.

Responsibilities Include But Are Not Limited To

Designing, implementing, and optimizing large-scale data ingest and processing systems in a Big Data environment
Installing, configuring, upgrading, and maintaining on-premises Elasticsearch clusters, including routine cluster health checks, shard allocation, index maintenance, and custom dashboard development for performance tuning and capacity planning
Designing, writing, and maintaining SaltStack states, pillars, and orchestration workflows to automate server provisioning, configuration compliance, and patch management across on-premises RHEL servers
Building and maintaining end-to-end CI/CD pipelines in GitLab CI and Jenkins that integrate automated builds, artifact publishing, and system deployments
Developing automation scripts in Bash, PowerShell, and Python for ad-hoc operational tasks, bulk provisioning, and monitoring plug-in development
Leading the integration of third-party software, prototyping emerging technologies through Proof-of-Concept initiatives, and establishing migration paths that minimize operational impact
Producing high-quality run-books, SOPs, architectural diagrams, and technical documentation in Confluence and Markdown while collaborating across engineering teams, vendors, and stakeholders

Minimum Qualifications

High School Diploma/GED with 4+ years of progressively responsible experience in platform engineering, data engineering, software development, or systems administration
2+ years of hands-on experience administering and patching RHEL/CentOS Linux servers in production, including server provisioning, configuration compliance, and hardware troubleshooting
2+ years of proven experience writing and maintaining SaltStack states, pillars, and orchestration workflows (or comparable IaC tools such as Ansible, Chef, or Puppet)
Demonstrated experience installing, configuring, upgrading, and troubleshooting Elasticsearch clusters, including Kibana, Beats, and Elastic Stack security features
Experience building and maintaining end-to-end CI/CD pipelines using GitLab CI, Jenkins, or similar automation tools to publish artifacts and drive automated deployments
Strong scripting experience and proficiency in Bash, Python, or PowerShell for workflow automation, bulk provisioning, and monitoring plug-in development
Experience integrating third-party software into existing infrastructure and producing comprehensive technical documentation, run-books, and SOPs in Confluence or Markdown

Preferred Qualifications

Advanced experience with large-scale Elasticsearch deployments, cluster health optimization, and multi-node scaling
Advanced proficiency in Configuration Management and Infrastructure as Code (IaC) utilizing SaltStack, Ansible, or Puppet
Practical knowledge of containerization and orchestration technologies, such as Docker and Kubernetes
Proven experience supporting mission-critical data operations and platform engineering initiatives within secure government environments

Clearance Requirements

An active TS/SCI with Polygraph is required for this position.

Physical Requirements

Must be able to remain in a stationary position 50% of the time.
Needs to occasionally move about inside the office to access file cabinets, office machinery, etc.
Frequently communicates with co-workers, management, and customers, which may involve delivering presentations. Must be able to exchange accurate information in these situations.

new_jobs.title: EDA Tools & Design Automation Engineer
new_jobs.description:
Tenstorrent is leading the industry on cutting-edge AI technology, revolutionizing performance expectations, ease of use, and cost efficiency. With AI redefining the computing paradigm, solutions must evolve to unify innovations in software models, compilers, platforms, networking, and semiconductors. Our diverse team of technologists have developed a high performance RISC-V CPU from scratch, and share a passion for AI and a deep desire to build the best AI platform possible. We value collaboration, curiosity, and a commitment to solving hard problems. We are growing our team and looking for contributors of all seniorities.

Tenstorrent is seeking an EDA Tools & Design Automation Engineer to join the Mixed Signal Design Automation team. In this role, you will own the deployment, configuration, reliability, and ongoing evolution of the EDA tool environment used by our mixed-signal design teams. You will develop and maintain AI-enabled design-automation tooling; build automation using Python and EDA-specific scripting languages; partner with CAD on tool and PDK configuration; and help define and support scalable EDA flows that enable faster, more reliable mixed-signal design iteration.

This role is remote,
based out of any location in North America
.

We welcome candidates at various experience levels. During the interview process, candidates will be assessed for the appropriate level, and offers will align with that level, which may differ from the one in this posting.

Who You Are

You have 5+ years of experience supporting, configuring, or automating semiconductor EDA tools in an analog, mixed-signal, custom-design, CAD, or methodology environment.
You’re a strong Python engineer with experience in Tcl and/or Cadence SKILL, Linux-based EDA environments, and GUI or batch-flow integrations.
You apply software best practices—including version control, code review, testing, CI/CD, documentation, and maintainable design—and have experience with AI-assisted development tools.
You’re analytical and collaborative, able to troubleshoot complex issues and work effectively with CAD, PDK, infrastructure, layout, and design teams. A relevant degree or equivalent practical experience is welcome.

What We Need

Own the deployment, configuration, reliability, and evolution of the EDA environment for Tenstorrent’s mixed-signal design teams.
Develop, test, release, and support AI-enabled automation and workflows, primarily in Python, with Tcl or Cadence SKILL integrations as needed.
Partner with Design Automation and CAD to build workflows, configure tools and PDKs, qualify supported versions, and maintain reproducible environments.
Help standardize automation conventions, interfaces, and data formats, and resolve tool, configuration, PDK, and workflow issues. Experience with Cadence and Synopsys custom flows, OpenAccess, verification, extraction, simulation, or Slurm/HPC is a plus.

What You Will Learn

How mixed-signal design teams use EDA tools and automation across the design lifecycle.
How to evolve AI-enabled workflows that support faster, more reliable design iteration.
How tool and PDK configurations, qualification, and reproducible environments enable scalable design flows.
How to balance standardization with flexibility across open-source, in-house, and commercial tools while collaborating across engineering teams.

Compensation for all engineers at Tenstorrent ranges from $100k - $500k including base and variable compensation targets. Experience, skills, education, background and location all impact the actual offer made.

Tenstorrent offers a highly competitive compensation package and benefits, and we are an equal opportunity employer.

Due to U.S. export laws, including those codified in the U.S. Export Administration Regulations (EAR), the Company is required to ensure compliance with these laws when transferring technology to nationals of certain countries (such as EAR Country Groups D:1, E1, and E2). These requirements apply to persons located in the U.S. and all countries outside the U.S. As the position offered will have direct and/or indirect access to information, systems, or technologies subject to these laws, the offer may be contingent upon your citizenship/permanent residency status or ability to obtain prior license approval from the U.S. Commerce Department or applicable federal agency. new_jobs.title: Test Automation Engineer
new_jobs.description:
Halvik Corp
delivers a wide range of services to 13 executive agencies and 15 independent agencies. Halvik is a highly successful WOB business with more than 50 prime contracts and 500+ professionals delivering Digital Services, Advanced Analytics, Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning, Cyber Security and Cutting-Edge Technology across the US Government. Be a part of something special!

Position Overview

Halvik is seeking a Test Automation Engineer to support the U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) Office of the Chief Digital & Information Officer (OCDIO) Digital Factory capacity task order. Operating under DOT's IT Modernization Initiative (ITIM-2025-007) and the 2025–2029 "Path to 1DOT IT" strategy, the program delivers modernized, secure, and resilient applications through a Software Factory, Capacity-as-a-Service (CaaS) model. Halvik provides Agile Scrum teams for Development, Modernization, and Enhancement (DME) work across cloud, on-premises, and SaaS platforms hosted within the USDOT IT security boundary.

As a member of Halvik's DME Scrum teams, the Test Automation Engineer designs, builds, and maintains automated test suites that are embedded in the CI/CD pipeline and run with every build and release. The program's Mandatory Iteration-Level Testing & Validation Framework makes testing a required delivery control and calls for a progressive shift from manual to automated execution. This role drives that shift. It contributes directly to the end-client's objectives by catching defects early, protecting existing functionality through automated regression, keeping defect rates within contract thresholds, and producing the objective test evidence needed for the Definition of Done, release readiness, and Authority to Operate (ATO) packages.

Core Responsibilities

Strategic Execution: Lead the development of a test automation strategy and reusable framework for each assigned product, prioritizing automation of smoke, regression, end-to-end, and high-risk scenarios, and progressively converting manual test cases to automated execution in line with the program's Automation Transition Requirement.
Operational Oversight: Manage daily execution, maintenance, and triage of automated test suites. Monitor results, isolate flaky tests, investigate failures, and log defects with clear reproduction steps and severity in the Government-furnished Jira instance.
Collaboration: Coordinate with developers, the Senior Business Analyst / QA Analyst, the Cloud Engineer / DevSecOps / CI-CD, the Solutions Architect, and the Scrum Master to turn user stories and acceptance criteria into automated tests, build testability into features, and deliver tested increments every sprint.
Technical Performance: Integrate automated tests into CI/CD pipelines (e.g., GitHub Enterprise, Azure DevOps) so that tests run on every build, deployment, and promotion, and make results available for sprint demos, release readiness reviews, and ATO evidence packages.
Government-Furnished Tools: Configure and operate OCDIO's automated testing tool (currently ClicTest) and any other Government-furnished testing tools, adapting quickly when tools change or new ones are provided.
Test Coverage Across Categories: Build and maintain automated coverage across the required testing categories, including smoke testing in every environment (with post-deployment validation in Production), end-to-end workflows across UI, APIs, and data layers, persona and role-based permissions, regression, and integration/API contract testing.
Performance, Security, and Accessibility Testing: Support automated performance and load validation under realistic transaction volumes, security checks aligned to the OWASP Top 10 and authentication/authorization rules, and automated Section 508 (WCAG 2.0 A/AA) accessibility scans.
Evidence and Definition of Done: Ensure objective test evidence (executed scripts, logs, automated output, and pass/fail results) is attached to the corresponding Jira ticket before any item is marked "Done," and document the rationale for any testing category that does not apply to a given change.
Quality Metrics: Track and report automation coverage, pass rates, and defect trends, and help keep the defect rate below the program's five percent Maximum Allowable Defect Rate (MADR) while supporting any corrective action planning.
Data and Release Validation: Develop automated scripts to validate data migrations (record counts, transformations, field-level mappings) and to verify deployment and rollback procedures before production promotion.

Minimum Requirements

Education: Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Technology, or a related field.
Experience: Minimum of 5 years of professional experience in software quality assurance, including at least 3 years designing and maintaining automated test frameworks for web applications and APIs within Agile Scrum teams.
Technical Proficiency: Advanced knowledge of test automation tools such as Selenium, Playwright, or Cypress; API testing tools such as Postman or REST Assured; at least one programming language used for automation (e.g., Java, C#, Python, or JavaScript/TypeScript); Git; CI/CD integration with GitHub Actions or Azure DevOps; and Jira for defect and test evidence tracking.
Compliance: Must meet U.S. DOT contract requirements, including a favorable Public Trust background investigation and suitability determination.
Certifications: ISTQB Certified Tester (Foundation Level or Test Automation Engineer) or an equivalent testing certification is preferred.
Security Clearance: DOT Public Trust Clearance

Preferred Expertise

Demonstrated success in Federal Contracting, particularly civilian agency IT modernization or Software Factory programs; prior DOT experience is a plus.
Familiarity with ClicTest or other low-code/codeless automation platforms, and with Agile/Scrum practices such as behavior-driven development (e.g., Cucumber, SpecFlow).
Experience with performance and load testing tools (e.g., JMeter, k6) and automated accessibility testing tools (e.g., axe, ANDI); DHS Trusted Tester certification is a plus.
Experience automating tests for enterprise platforms used at DOT, such as Salesforce, Microsoft Power Platform, ServiceNow, Dynamics 365, or Appian.
Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities.

new_jobs.title: Sr Data Engineer
new_jobs.description:
The work we do has an impact on millions of lives, and you can be a part of it.

We help protect our customers against life’s uncertainties. Regardless of where you work within the company, you’ll be helping provide protection and peace of mind when our customers need it most.

Protective is looking for Data Engineers to design, build, and operate production data pipelines on Voyager, our Databricks lakehouse on Azure. You will own the end-to-end flow of data through a medallion architecture — ingesting source data into the Bronze layer, applying cleansing, validation, and conformance in Silver, and publishing trusted, consumption-ready data products in Gold.

This role sits at the intersection of engineering, analytics, and platform operations. You will write production-grade Python and SQL, enforce data contracts, and help Protective treat data as a product with named owners and real consumers. You will be embedded on a delivery pod that owns its data products end to end, rather than servicing tickets from a queue.

On Voyager, the medallion layers are named Raw, Prep, and Prod. They map directly to Bronze, Silver, and Gold and are used interchangeably in this description.

Key Responsibilities

Design, develop, and maintain production data pipelines on Databricks using Python, SQL, Apache Spark, and Delta Lake
Build Bronze-layer ingestion that reliably captures data from APIs, relational databases, flat files, cloud storage, and SaaS platforms — using dlt (dltHub) and Databricks-native ingestion where each fits — including incremental loading, pagination, watermarking, state management, and replay after failure
Develop Silver-layer transformations in dbt and Python over Delta Lake that cleanse, standardize, type, deduplicate, validate, conform, and enrich data so that it is reusable across domains. A meaningful share of this role is making messy source data trustworthy
Create Gold-layer data products: dimensional models, slowly changing dimensions, fact and bridge tables, aggregates, and serving tables aligned to how consumers actually query
Produce and maintain the curated datasets ML engineering trains and serves models from — feature and training tables that are versioned and reproducible, not one-off extracts
Author and maintain data contracts using the Open Data Contract Standard (ODCS) — schema with real semantics, named owner, known consumers, quality rules, and freshness expectations — and assess backward compatibility before every change
Implement data quality as code: uniqueness and not-null on keys at minimum, plus referential, accepted-value, freshness, and custom business-rule tests, surfaced to producers and consumers rather than buried in logs
Orchestrate ingestion and transformation as assets in Dagster, deployed to Dagster Cloud, and operate what you build across development, branch, and production deployments — schedules and sensors, asset dependencies, backfills, and run observability
Apply governance through Unity Catalog — catalogs, schemas, external locations, grants, row- and column-level security, and lineage — and handle credentials through Azure Key Vault rather than in code
Implement incremental and merge-based processing with Delta Lake (MERGE, schema evolution, time travel, OPTIMIZE) and tune Spark jobs, table layouts, and compute for performance and cost
Troubleshoot production failures, data-quality issues, source-system changes, and late-arriving or duplicate data — including backfills and recovery — and take part in the pod’s on-call rotation for the pipelines it owns, with root-cause analysis that closes the gap rather than reopening the ticket
Build and maintain CI/CD for data assets in Azure DevOps — automated tests and CI checks on dlt, dbt, and Dagster changes, promotion from development through branch deployments to production, and releases that are repeatable and auditable
Instrument what you own for observability: freshness, volume, quality, latency, and cost, with alerting tied to the SLAs and SLOs your contract commits to instead of depending on someone noticing
Work inside the platform’s control expectations — least-privilege access, secrets in Azure Key Vault, change management through pull request and pipeline, and audit evidence that falls out of the deployment path rather than being reconstructed later
Participate in code review and document architecture, runbooks, and data products so others can discover, trust, and reuse them
Work with data architects, analysts, product owners, and business stakeholders to translate requirements into maintainable data solutions

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related field; equivalent practical experience considered
3+ years building and supporting production data pipelines in a cloud data platform environment
Strong hands-on Python and SQL. Both are used daily and neither substitutes for the other
Hands-on experience with Databricks or a comparable Spark-based lakehouse, including Delta Lake tables, MERGE, and incremental load patterns
Practical understanding of medallion / multi-layer lakehouse design, and the judgment to say what belongs in Bronze versus Silver versus Gold
Experience ingesting data from APIs, relational databases, files, or SaaS applications, including the incremental and state-management problems that come with it
Working knowledge of dimensional modeling — grain, keys, facts and dimensions, slowly changing dimensions — and of ELT design patterns and data quality practice
Experience with orchestration and scheduling using Dagster, Databricks Workflows, Airflow, Azure Data Factory, or similar
Git-based source control, pull request review, automated testing, and CI/CD as normal practice — Azure DevOps or comparable
Experience troubleshooting production data failures, performance bottlenecks, and source-system changes
Experience with pipeline monitoring and alerting, and a working understanding of what a freshness or quality SLA means once real consumers depend on it
Ability to explain technical designs and trade-offs to both technical and non-technical partners

Preferred Qualifications

Databricks certification (Data Engineer Associate or Professional) or equivalent demonstrated depth
Unity Catalog experience: catalogs, schemas, volumes, external locations, storage credentials, permissions, and lineage
dbt on Databricks, or another transformation framework used alongside Spark
Python-based modeling frameworks over Delta Lake, and experience implementing Type 2 history, surrogate keys, and merge strategies in code
Experience with a declarative Python ingestion framework such as dlt (dltHub), Airbyte, Meltano, or Fivetran
Dagster experience specifically, including assets, asset checks, sensors, schedules, and branch deployments

We aim to protect the wellbeing of our employees and their families with a broad benefits offering. In addition to offering comprehensive health, dental and vision insurance, we support emotional wellbeing through mental health benefits and an employee assistance program. Work/life balance is important and Protective offers a variety of paid time away benefits ( e.g. , paid time off, paid parental leave, short-term disability, and a cultural observance day). The financial health of our employees is just as important as physical and emotional health. Some of the financial wellbeing benefits include contributions to healthcare accounts, a pension plan, and a 401(k) plan with Company matching. All employees are encouraged to protect their overall wellbeing by engaging in ProHealth Rewards, Protective’s platform to improve wellbeing while earning cash rewards.

The AI-Native Software Engineer
will be responsible for shipping, evaluating, securing, and supporting real systems. The ideal candidate is a strong engineer who has real hands-on experience using AI to build and ship production-quality software. They should be able to use AI agents and coding assistants across the SDLC: planning, design, codebase analysis, implementation, testing, documentation, code review, refactoring, deployment, and production support.

How You Will Make An Impact

Development on agentic AI engineering technology.
Daily or weekly use of AI coding tools such as GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Claude Code, ChatGPT, Codex-style agents, or similar.
Model evaluation and quality measurement.
Maintains active relationships with internal and/or external stakeholder to develop business requirements.
Analyzes and classifies complex change request and identifies and documents possible system code enhancements.
Demonstrates knowledge of industry trends, responsible AI, data privacy, and secure handling of sensitive information.
Collaborates with engineers and graphic designers, analyzes and classifies complex change request and reviews and evaluates possible enhancements.
Works with development team to develop and define application scope and objectives and prepare functional and/or technical specifications.
Analyzes and evaluates detailed business and technical requirements.
Understands the product and analytics and drive requirements that take into account stakeholders needs.
Identifies problems/risks.
Codes and maintains complex components of information systems.
Mentors others on coding standards and performs code reviews.
Reviews test cases and advises QA on adjacent code/regression impact.
Develops and performs system testing and fixes defects identified during testing and re-executes unit tests to validate results.
Aids in integrating activities with other IT departments for successful implementation and support of project efforts.
Provides on call support and monitors the system and identifies system deficiencies.

Minimum Requirements

Requires an BA/BS degree in Information Technology, Computer Science or related field of study and a minimum of 3 years experience on one platform, multi database, multi language or multi business application; or any combination of education and experience, which would provide an equivalent background.

Preferred Skills, Capabilities And Experiences

Experience with healthcare, payer, claims, clinical, HIPAA, PHI, regulated industry, or enterprise security experience.
Strong software engineering fundamentals including, cloud-native development, APIs and microservices, CI/CD, automated testing, and secure SDLC strongly preferred.
Experience building or integrating AI agents, tool/function calling, RAG, memory, model routing, evaluations, guardrails, observability, and secure API/tool access strongly preferred.
Experience with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, including AgentCore Runtime, Memory, Identity, Gateway, Code Interpreter, Browser Tool, Observability, Evaluations, and Policy and is strongly preferred.
Experience building LLM or SLM applications.
Ability to review, test, and harden AI-generated code.
Production support experience.
